items.title: AMDockVS
items.text: AMDockVS is a chemistry-focused desktop application and Python API for molecular import, preparation, QSAR, binding-site analysis, docking, and result inspection. It uses MolSuite for projects, task orchestration, executors, and data flow.
path: Home

items.title: Install
items.text:
AMDockVS requires Python 3.12. The MolSuite packages and PyMOL (the pymol-open-source alpha wheels, through ms_components) are installed automatically from PyPI, so no conda environment is needed:

python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install AMDockVS

Start the desktop application with:

amdockvs
path: Home

items.title: The global selection
items.text:
Right-click rows in a Ligands or Receptors table and choose Select to work on just those rows. The selection is global: there is one for ligands and one for receptors, and every table and tool of that role (Build, Docking Studio, including Preview & Run) works on it, whichever one it was made in. A tool that offers its own choice of what to work on, such as Diversity, uses the selection only under Current selection; any other choice there ignores it.

While a selection is active the status bar shows it, for example Ligands: 2 selected ✕, and the ID column of the table is marked as filtered. Nothing clears it for you: it survives preparing and docking, so a run can be repeated on the same rows. Click the status-bar entry to drop it and go back to the whole library.
path: Home

items.title: Python API
items.text:
The supported entry point is deliberately small:

from amdockvs import AMDockVSRuntime

runtime = AMDockVSRuntime()
try:
    project = runtime.create_or_open_project(
        name="screening",
        folder="./screening-project",
    )
    print(project)
finally:
    runtime.shutdown()

The runtime groups operations by domain:

Namespace Responsibility runtime.loader Ligand and receptor import runtime.molecules Queries, scopes, filters, and saved sets runtime.chemistry Ligand and receptor preparation runtime.complexes Explicit receptor-ligand relationships runtime.qsar Activities, descriptors, models, and predictions runtime.binding_sites Manual sites and P2Rank predictions runtime.docking Preparation, grids, docking with Vina, QuickVina 2, gnina or AutoDock-GPU, and results runtime.diversity Clustering and representative selection runtime.tools External tools: status, install, repair

Continue with the API guide, copy a complete example, or browse the generated API reference.

items.title: Preparación de receptores (anotado 2026-09-01)
items.text:
Tres bugs verificados con 4UWH (p2). Los tres reparados 2026-09-01: el escritor de io/receptor_preview.py ya no aplica su lista blanca ciega, y qué llega al PDBQT se decide ahora en Docking Studio > Receptors ("Include structural waters" / "Include cofactors", apagadas por defecto). Cubierto por test/test_receptor_hetero.py.

  1. ~~remove_cofactors no hace nada — io/receptor_preview.py:315~~ DONE 2026-09-01 _components_to_remove() ya decidía bien, pero el escritor aplicaba después if not _is_polymer_residue(resname) and resname not in _COORDINATION_METAL_CODES: continue, así que los cofactores se borraban siempre, marcada o no la casilla. Meeko los prepara sin problema: probado con JXM (30 átomos) → PDBQT con 31. Reparado: el filtro es ahora "lo que no está en component_keys", y clasifica por resname (no por residue_key: una assembly biológica renombra las cadenas copiadas).

  2. ~~remove_non_structural_waters no hace nada — io/receptor_preview.py:317~~ DONE 2026-09-01 Se borraban todas las aguas, incluidas las estructurales que la preview marca como is_selected. Meeko sí las admite: con coordenadas reales salen al PDBQT como OW/HW1/HW2 tipo OA/HD y cargas TIP3P (-0.412 / +0.206). Ojo al depurar: aguas con coordenadas inventadas que solapan la proteína hacen que Meeko falle con adjacent_mol doesn't contain the mapped atoms (enlaces inter-residuo espurios), no es un problema de soporte de agua.

  3. ~~retained_structural_waters miente y nadie lo consume — io/receptor_preview.py:331~~ DONE 2026-09-01 a medias: ya no miente (con (2) reparado, las aguas retenidas están de verdad en el fichero), pero el campo sigue sin consumidor. Borrarlo cuando se decida que nadie lo va a leer.

items.title: Interacciones en la tabla (anotado 2026-10-08)
items.text:
Decidido por Mario; no se trabaja hasta cerrar el motor de orquestación (ms_flow).

  • Las interacciones viven en interaction_results. Hoy la casilla del docking (compute_diagram) solo deja <pose>.rank<N>.diagram.json + imagen junto a la pose y la tabla queda vacía; solo la llena amdock_interactions_job.
  • Docking con la opción marcada: una sola task que devuelve filas para docking_results e interaction_results por un graph_sink (la fila hija lleva la referencia a su pose y el sink pone docking_result_id).
  • Decidido 2026-10-17: interaction_results se identifica por (payload del receptor, payload de la pose del ligando), no por docking_result_id. Así un complejo de referencia (cocristal, sin fila de docking) tiene su diagrama con la misma tabla, sin otra estructura. El docking escribe la fila con los payloads que ya conoce; no hace falta la relación del graph_sink hacia docking_results.
  • No se filtra por interacciones (consultas tipo "poses con puente de H a ASP86"): solo se guardan y se muestran. Quizás más adelante; no se diseña para ello ahora.
  • La imagen no se genera en el docking: el diagrama se dibuja en la UI a partir de las interacciones. Si algún día hace falta, se añade.
  • El panel de resultados lee las interacciones de la tabla (list_interactions), no del JSON (pose_interactions, ui/catalog/results.py:864): el fichero puede no estar.
  • El botón "Build diagram" y amdock_diagram_job detectan y no escriben en la tabla: arreglar.
  • Depende de ms_contactmap (en desarrollo): entrada solo de detección y SASA más rápido. Medido el 2026-10-08 en una pose (1iep): detección 0,04 s; exposición 3,0 s; layout 0,15 s; imagen 1,8 s. El job de interacciones paga hoy esos 3 s porque llama a build_pose_diagram (docking/results/interactions.py:57).

items.title: Editar un receptor ya importado (anotado 2026-10-15)
items.text:
• Hoy cadenas, ensamblaje, altloc, aguas y cofactores quedan fijados al importar; no hay acción para cambiarlos. Reimportar el mismo archivo con otras opciones crea una variante nueva (otra clave de almacenamiento, _receptor_import_variant), no reemplaza. Los binding sites sí se editan después (herramienta Binding Sites).
  • Todo lo necesario para reprocesar ya se guarda: la copia del original (original_path) y las opciones usadas (extra_data.structure.import_profile).
  • Propuesta: acción de fila "Edit import…" que abre el panel de importación con esa fila rellenada; al aplicar, "Edit a copy" (variante nueva) o "Replace" (mismo patrón que el editor Ketcher de ligandos). "Replace" avisa de que se borran dockings, binding sites y preparaciones que dependen del receptor.

items.title: Duplicados en Ligands (anotado 2026-10-17)
items.text:
• Hoy el import no detecta duplicados: el mismo compuesto importado dos veces son dos filas y se dockea dos veces (pasó con datos duplicados a propósito para hacer crecer la tabla).
  • No comprobarlo en el import (coste por molécula en el camino caliente). molecules.inchikey ya existe y tiene índice: detectarlos después es un GROUP BY inchikey HAVING count(*) > 1.
  • Forma propuesta: acción "Find duplicates" en Ligands que filtra/selecciona las repetidas (como un scope), y el usuario decide borrar o conservar. Opcional: aviso al terminar el import si la consulta encuentra alguna. Sin implementar.

items.title: Cross-docking (anotado 2026-10-17)
items.text:
• Redocking dockea cada ligando de referencia en SU receptor (el par original del complejo). Cross-docking: cada ligando de referencia contra los receptores de OTROS complejos del mismo blanco, para medir si el protocolo reproduce poses con una conformación de proteína ajena.
  • Lo que falta: elegir el conjunto de receptores (mismos binding sites / misma proteína), superponer cada receptor sobre el del complejo original para que el RMSD contra el ligando de referencia tenga sentido (hoy el RMSD se mide en el marco del receptor dockeado), y una vista de resultados en matriz ligando × receptor (éxito ≤ 2 Å).
  • Encaja como otro run_kind sobre el mismo motor de docking. Sin implementar.

items.title: Almacenamiento del docking (anotado 2026-10-19)
items.text:
Sale del benchmark docs/benchmarks/vs_classic_2026-10-18/. Hoy son 27 KB por ligando con 9 poses (~890 GB para 33 M). Por pose, docking_results.metrics lleva 1199 B de JSON: 551 B del run, 352 B del ligando, 247 B derivados del score y solo 49 B que son de la pose.

  • Configuración del run una sola vez: caja, protocolo, engine, backend, exhaustiveness, run_id, fecha y receptor van en una tabla de runs (o en un volumen si es grande), y cada fila la referencia por id.
  • Propiedades del ligando fuera de docking_results: MW, TPSA, cLogP, HBD/HBA y átomos pesados ya están en molecules. Las 9 energías del ligando se repiten en cada una de sus poses.
  • Derivados del score (LE, pKi, BEI, SEI, LLE…): se quedan, porque se usan para ordenar y filtrar. Son ligeros, pero mejor como columnas que dentro del JSON. lle y lipophilic_efficiency son el mismo valor dos veces.
  • Limpieza profunda de lo duplicado o sin uso: índices repetidos (idx_dr_ligand_molecule = ix_docking_results_ligand_molecule_id, idx_dr_receptor_molecule = ix_docking_results_receptor_molecule_id), tablas sin uso y propiedades que están en 3 o 4 sitios.
  • ¿Hacen falta 9 poses? En VS bastaría probablemente con el top 3. Antes de fijarlo, medir con rescoring de gnina en qué posición original cae la pose que gana.
  • Compresión de poses: cada pose es un payload aparte (SDF con todos los H, ~3,9 KB, zstd sin diccionario → 848 B). Medido con las 4446 poses: zstd-19 sin diccionario 784 B, con diccionario entrenado (PayloadStore.train_dictionary ya existe y AMDockVS no lo usa) 566 B, todas como un solo bloque 416 B. Guardar la topología una vez por ligando y solo las coordenadas por pose: medido en docs/benchmarks/vs_classic_2026-10-18/ (un payload por ligando = 50 %; int16 a 1e-3 Å = 33 %; solo átomos pesados = 20 % de lo de hoy). Propuesta (2026-10-19, sin decidir): lo genérico es un payload por ligando con sus poses en el formato de hoy (SDF de varias moléculas, PDB/PDBQT con MODEL). Sirve para cualquier tipo de molécula y da el 50 %. int32 sin pérdida da lo mismo (49 %), y un diccionario zstd no aporta nada con bloques agrupados (51 %). Las coordenadas int16 (33 %) solo valen la pena para el modo shards.
  • "Fire and forget" con corte de energía, como en shards: el usuario fija un corte (p. ej. −8,5 para Vina y derivados) y no se guardan en disco las poses de los ligandos peores que el corte (score > −8,5). Solo queda su registro de energía en la tabla. Sin implementar.

items.title: AMDock Performance Scenarios
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: Objetivo
items.text:
Validar AMDock con escenarios del dominio, no con jobs sintéticos aislados.

La carga relevante para esta app es:

  • ingestión de muchos ligandos desde varios archivos
  • cálculo de descriptores sobre tablas grandes del proyecto
  • docking mock con muchos pares ligando-receptor y muchos outputs en disco
  • ejecución concurrente de varios jobs dentro del mismo proyecto
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: Escenarios canónicos
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: 1. Small interactive
items.text:
• decenas de ligandos
  • 1 receptor
  • feedback rápido
  • uso típico: depuración o exploración manual

Política recomendada: latency
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: 2. Balanced workstation
items.text:
• cientos de ligandos
  • 1-2 receptores
  • mezcla razonable entre feedback y throughput
  • uso típico: flujo diario de escritorio

Política recomendada: balanced
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: 3. Throughput screening
items.text:
• cientos o miles de ligandos
  • múltiples archivos de entrada
  • 2 o más receptores
  • resultados voluminosos en docking_results

Política recomendada: throughput
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: 4. Cancellation under load
items.text:
• job largo de import o docking
  • cancelación pedida desde monitor o runtime
  • verificación de visibilidad operativa y cierre limpio

Estado actual:

  • el escenario está definido y cubierto a nivel de contrato operativo del monitor
  • todavía no hay una prueba pesada dedicada solo a cancelación de screening
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: Políticas ajustadas
items.text:
El banco de pruebas define tres perfiles en tools/screening_benchmark.py (fuera del paquete desde 2026-08-29: ningun job de AMDock los declara, solo los mide el benchmark):

  • latency
  • import_batch_size=250
  • descriptor_batch_size=250
  • docking_batch_size=64
  • balanced
  • import_batch_size=1000
  • descriptor_batch_size=1000
  • docking_batch_size=128
  • throughput
  • import_batch_size=2000
  • descriptor_batch_size=1500
  • docking_batch_size=256
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: Criterio de tuning
items.text:
Las decisiones de AMDock a nivel app se concentran en batch_size.

No se introdujo una política propia de flush o retention en la app porque:

  • los sinks ya están resueltos por MolSuite
  • la retención durable pertenece al contrato del executor, no al dominio de AMDock
  • cambiar flush/retention en AMDock sin presión real de datos duplicaría knobs del engine

En esta fase, el ajuste serio y defendible fue:

  • fijar perfiles de batching explícitos
  • validarlos con benchmark de screening real
  • usar el perfil throughput en la prueba e2e de carga más pesada
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: Validación actual
items.text:
• benchmark de screening con conteos y throughput medidos
  • importación concurrente desde dos SDF
  • screening más pesado con perfil throughput

Eso deja la app en un punto razonable para seguir con dominio/UI sin improvisar tamaños de lote.
path: AMDock Performance Scenarios

items.title: Estructura recomendada de amdock
items.text: Esta app se está migrando a una forma más simple e intuitiva. La prioridad no es “la arquitectura más pura”, sino que un programador nuevo pueda abrir ../src/amdockvs y entender rápido dónde tocar.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

items.title: Regla principal
items.text:
La ruta feliz debe estar en pocos sitios:

  • runtime.py: fachada pública de negocio
  • jobs/: jobs y tasks por funcionalidad
  • queries.py: lecturas de dominio del proyecto
  • io/: parsing y materialización de archivos
  • summaries.py: DTOs públicos

La UI no debe esconder lógica de negocio. Debe llamar al runtime.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

items.title: Excepción deliberada: docking
items.text:
Docking sí tiene variación real y frecuente. Por eso su extensión se concentra en src/amdockvs/docking/ mediante tres contratos pequeños, sin crear un framework de plugins adicional:

  • programs.py: capacidades, modelo de configuración y recursos del programa.
  • preparations.py: perfil de preparación de ligando, receptor y, opcionalmente, shard.
  • registry.py: registro y despacho del runner que ejecuta un chunk.
  • vina.py, qvina.py, gnina.py, adgpu.py: implementación de cada runner incorporado; autogrid.py genera los mapas AD4 que comparten Vina (ad4) y AutoDock-GPU.

Los jobs de MolSuite (preparation_jobs.py, jobs.py y shard_jobs.py) son la infraestructura estable. No deben importar condicionalmente cada engine ni contener ramas if engine == ...; reciben el nombre registrado y despachan por los contratos anteriores. Los nombres históricos de task de Vina se conservan únicamente para no romper jobs persistidos.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

items.title: Añadir un docking engine
items.text:
Un engine nuevo define un modelo Pydantic propio, un DockingProgramSpec y un runner:

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from amdockvs.docking import DockingProgramSpec, register_docking_engine


class MyEngineConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    iterations: int = Field(default=20, ge=1)


MY_ENGINE = DockingProgramSpec(
    key="my_engine",
    label="My engine",
    workflow_key="vina",
    preparation_engine="ad4",
    docking_engine="my_engine",
    config_model=MyEngineConfig,
    protocol_identity_keys=("iterations",),
    resource_resolver=lambda config: {"cpu_required": 2},
)


def run_my_engine(payload: dict) -> list[dict]:
    # payload["pairs"] contiene los pares resueltos por el job de MolSuite.
    # payload["iterations"] ya fue validado y combinado desde engine_config.
    ...


register_docking_engine(MY_ENGINE, run_my_engine)

Las capacidades requires_ligand_preparation, requires_receptor_preparation y requires_binding_site controlan readiness y construcción de lotes. supports_shards debe declararse solo si el runner acepta el contrato de campañas por shards.

Si la preparación no es ad4, se registra junto al programa:

from amdockvs.docking import PreparationProfile, register_preparation_profile

register_preparation_profile(
    PreparationProfile(
        key="my_prep",
        prepare_entities=prepare_my_entities,
        prepare_shard=prepare_my_shard,  # opcional
    )
)

Vina, QuickVina, GNINA y AutoDock-GPU comparten correctamente el perfil ad4: los cuatro consumen PDBQT compatible. Compartir la preparación evita duplicación; no implica compartir el runner ni la configuración del docking.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

items.title: Regla de contexto
items.text:
AMDock no resuelve layout del proyecto por su cuenta.

Las rutas de trabajo salen del contrato de MolSuite:

  • ligands
  • receptors
  • docking_results
  • exports
  • jobs

Los jobs deben consumir project_resources desde config, no recomponer data/... o results/... localmente.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

items.title: Qué va junto
items.text:
Cada feature del backend debe vivir junta:

  • jobs/ingestion.py
  • jobs/descriptors.py
  • jobs/docking.py

En cada módulo de jobs/ se permite tener:

  • modelos Params
  • helpers pequeños propios del job
  • @task(...)
  • @job(...)

Esto evita perseguir el flujo entre job.py, task.py, service.py, builder.py y registry.py cuando todavía no hace falta.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

items.title: Qué no hacer por ahora
items.text:
No crear capas preventivas tipo:

  • repository/
  • services/
  • builders/
  • orchestrators/
  • domain/infra/application/ artificial

Solo merece separarse si un módulo deja de ser legible por sí mismo o si una pieza se reutiliza claramente entre varias features.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

items.title: Criterio de separación
items.text:
Separar un módulo cuando ocurra una de estas:

  • supera un tamaño que ya dificulta leer el flujo completo
  • mezcla dos responsabilidades reales distintas
  • una función se reutiliza desde más de una feature
  • una dependencia pesada merece quedar aislada, como I/O o parsing

Por eso io/loaders.py sí tiene sentido aparte: no es “arquitectura extra”, es una frontera real entre parsing/materialización y jobs. El layout del proyecto no vive ahí; vive en MolSuite.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

items.title: Cómo debería verse un caso de uso nuevo
items.text:
Si mañana añadimos un job de scoring posterior a docking, la ruta esperada sería:

  • jobs/scoring.py
  • método público en runtime.py
  • lecturas de resultados en queries.py si hacen falta
  • DTO nuevo en summaries.py solo si la API pública lo necesita

No debería requerir crear un subárbol entero nuevo.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

items.title: Contrato mental para el equipo
items.text:
• Si quiero ejecutar algo de dominio: voy a runtime.py
  • Si quiero cambiar cómo se define un job: voy a jobs/
  • Si quiero cambiar cómo se leen datos del proyecto: voy a queries.py
  • Si quiero tocar parsing o archivos: voy a io/
  • Si quiero saber qué devuelve la API: voy a summaries.py
  • Si quiero construir una vista de dominio: voy a ui/, pero consumo runtime.py, no molsuite.core.* ni SQL directo

Ese mapa es más valioso para esta app que una separación demasiado sofisticada.
path: Estructura recomendada de amdock

submit_job(job, *, params: Any = None, executor_name: Optional[str] = None, cpu_required: Optional[int] = None, max_job_cpu: Optional[int] = None, max_inflight_tasks: Optional[int] = None, total_chunks: Optional[int] = None, depends_on: Optional[list[str]] = None, priority: int = 0, result_handler_kwargs: Optional[dict] = None, auto_depends: bool = True) -> str

Submit a job, auto-waiting for active prerequisite jobs by default.

With auto_depends=True (default) the job is held until every active job of its prerequisite categories finishes, so a deferred pipeline can be queued at once. Pass auto_depends=False to submit immediately regardless of running jobs. Returns the key of the job in the project's journal, which is its id everywhere here.

Source code in src/amdockvs/runtime.py 
def submit_job(
    self,
    job,
    *,
    params: Any = None,
    executor_name: Optional[str] = None,
    cpu_required: Optional[int] = None,
    max_job_cpu: Optional[int] = None,
    max_inflight_tasks: Optional[int] = None,
    total_chunks: Optional[int] = None,
    depends_on: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    priority: int = 0,
    result_handler_kwargs: Optional[dict] = None,
    auto_depends: bool = True,
) -> str:
    """Submit a job, auto-waiting for active prerequisite jobs by default.

    With auto_depends=True (default) the job is held until every active job of its
    prerequisite categories finishes, so a deferred pipeline can be queued at once.
    Pass auto_depends=False to submit immediately regardless of running jobs.
    Returns the key of the job in the project's journal, which is its id everywhere here.
    """
    self._require_active_project()
    depends_on = list(depends_on or [])
    depends_on += [job_id for job_id in getattr(self, "_forced_dependencies", None) or () if job_id not in depends_on]
    if auto_depends:
        depends_on = self.resolve_job_dependencies(job, depends_on) or []
    workspace = self.workspace
    job_config = self._job_config()
    engine_job, on_error = job.engine_job(handler_kwargs=result_handler_kwargs)
    job_params = job.validate_params(params)
    total = total_chunks if total_chunks is not None else job.count_chunks(job_params, config=job_config)
    job_id = uuid4().hex
    engine_ids = self._engine_ids()
    engine_ids[job_id] = workspace.submit(
        engine_job,
        job_params,
        key=job_id,
        executor=self._run_on(job, executor_name),
        # A job that ended in an earlier session has nothing left to wait for.
        after=[engine_ids[dep] for dep in depends_on if dep in engine_ids],
        total=total,
        cpu=cpu_required,
        window=max_inflight_tasks,
        max_cpu=max_job_cpu,
        priority=priority,
        on_error=on_error,
        **({"thread": True} if job.on_thread is not None and job.on_thread(job_params) else {}),
    )
    # Single funnel for "a job just started" UI feedback (the main window plugs a toast in
    # here). May fire from a worker thread, so the hook must be thread-safe (a Qt signal).
    hook = getattr(self, "on_job_submitted", None)
    if hook is not None:
        try:
            hook(str(getattr(job, "name", "") or "Job"), job_id)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - feedback must never break a submit
            pass
    return job_id

Continue a job that was canceled or interrupted, on executor_name or where it was.

A job that is still running is canceled first and waited for, which is how it is moved to another executor: not from a thread that cannot wait. It waits for the jobs its kind waits for, as when it was submitted.

Source code in src/amdockvs/runtime.py 
def resume_job(self, job_id: str, executor_name: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """Continue a job that was canceled or interrupted, on `executor_name` or where it was.

    A job that is still running is canceled first and waited for, which is how it is moved
    to another executor: not from a thread that cannot wait. It waits for the jobs its kind
    waits for, as when it was submitted.
    """
    self._require_active_project()
    job_id = str(job_id)
    job, was_on = self._recorded_job(job_id)
    executor = self._run_on(job, executor_name or was_on)
    self._job_config()
    engine_ids = self._engine_ids()
    waits = [engine_ids[dep] for dep in self.resolve_job_dependencies(job) or ()
             if dep in engine_ids and dep != job_id]
    engine_ids[job_id] = self.workspace.move(job_id, executor, after=waits)
    return job_id

def resolve_job_dependencies(self, job, explicit: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> Optional[list[str]]:
    """Union of explicit depends_on and the ids of active jobs this one should wait for."""
    category = _job_category(getattr(job, "name", "") or "")
    prereqs = _JOB_PREREQS.get(category or "", ())
    deps: list[str] = list(explicit or [])
    if prereqs or category == "chemistry":
        for status in self.list_jobs(statuses=NON_TERMINAL_JOB_STATUSES):
            active_category = _job_category(status.task_type)
            serial_chemistry = category == "chemistry" and active_category == "chemistry"
            if (active_category in prereqs or serial_chemistry) and status.job_id not in deps:
                deps.append(status.job_id)
    return deps or None

def wait_for_job(self, job_id: str, *, poll_s: float = 0.2) -> JobStatus:
    """Block until the job has ended. `poll_s` is not used: the engine tells."""
    self._require_active_project()
    engine_id = self._engine_ids().get(str(job_id))
    if engine_id is None:  # of an earlier session: it ended with it
        status = self.get_job_status(job_id)
        if status is None:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown job: {job_id}")
        return status
    return self._job_status_from_snapshot(self.workspace.engine.wait(engine_id))

def watch_jobs(self, job_ids: Iterable[str], *, poll_s: float = 0.2) -> dict[str, JobStatus]:
    """Display concurrent tqdm progress for several jobs of this session."""
    self._require_active_project()

def run_destinations(self, job=None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Where a job may be sent now, as (executor_name, label): the executors that are
    active, the default one first. With `job`, only the ones that job can run on.
    """
    self._require_active_project()
    rows = [row for row in self.workspace.executors() if row["state"] == "on"]
    # ponytail: `hpc` in the old list of a job is what says its worker needs nothing of
    # this machine but its payload and the files marked in it; one flag when the lists go.
    if job is not None and "hpc" not in job.supported_executors:
        rows = [row for row in rows if row["hosts"] == ["local"]]
    return [(row["name"], row["name"]) for row in sorted(rows, key=lambda row: not row["default"])]

def excluded_since(self, before: set[int], *, limit: int = 10_000) -> list[tuple[int, str, str]]:
    """``(id, name, reason)`` of the molecules excluded now but not in ``before`` — what a run
    failed. ponytail: a run alongside it mixes its failures in; per-job ids if that matters."""
    new = sorted(self.excluded_ids() - set(before))[: int(limit)]
    if not new:
        return []
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        rows = session.exec(
            select(MoleculeRecord.id, MoleculeRecord.name, MoleculeRecord.exclusion_reason)
            .where(MoleculeRecord.id.in_(new))
            .order_by(MoleculeRecord.id)
        ).all()
    return [(int(i), str(name or ""), str(reason or "")) for i, name, reason in rows]

def details(self, molecule_id: int) -> Details | None:
    """Load the complete Details-panel projection for a molecule."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    resolved_id = int(molecule_id)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        molecule = session.get(MoleculeRecord, resolved_id)
        if molecule is None:
            return None
        binding_sites = tuple(session.exec(
            select(BindingSite)
            .where(BindingSite.molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .order_by(BindingSite.id)
        ).all())
        receptor_complexes = tuple(session.exec(
            select(ComplexRecord)
            .where(ComplexRecord.receptor_molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .order_by(ComplexRecord.id.desc())
        ).all())
        ligand_complexes = tuple(session.exec(
            select(ComplexRecord)
            .where(ComplexRecord.ligand_molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .order_by(ComplexRecord.id.desc())
        ).all())
        activities = tuple(session.exec(
            select(LigandActivity)
            .where(LigandActivity.molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .order_by(LigandActivity.id.desc())
        ).all())
        structure = molecule_payload_id(molecule)
        current_model = None if structure is None else session.exec(
            select(MoleculeModel)
            .where(MoleculeModel.molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .where(MoleculeModel.payload_id == int(structure))
        ).first()
    model_data = None
    if current_model is not None and current_model.data_payload_id is not None:
        import json

        from amdockvs.core.payloads import read_structure

        model_data = json.loads(read_structure(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, current_model.data_payload_id)[0])
        model_data.pop("pae", None)
    return self.Details(
        molecule=molecule,
        binding_sites=binding_sites,
        receptor_complexes=receptor_complexes,
        ligand_complexes=ligand_complexes,
        activities=activities,
        current_model=current_model,
        current_model_data=model_data,
    )

    from amdockvs.molecules import filtering as filter_sql

    normalized_action = str(action or "").strip().lower()
    if normalized_action not in {"enrich", "recover", "tag"}:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported molecule-filter action: {action!r}")
    conditions = filter_sql.scope_conditions(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, as_molecule_scope(scope))
    prefix = str(exclusion_reason_prefix or "").strip()
    if prefix:
        conditions.append(MoleculeRecord.exclusion_reason.like(f"{prefix}%"))
    if normalized_action == "tag":
        ids = filter_sql.matched_ids(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, conditions, criteria)
        ref = self.create_set(
            ids,
            name=set_name,
            kind="filter",
            metadata={"source": str(reason or "")},
        )
        return len(ids), int(ref.id)
    return filter_sql.apply_state(
        self.runtime.workspace.project_db,
        conditions,
        criteria,
        activate_matches=normalized_action == "recover",
        exclude_nonmatches=normalized_action == "enrich",
        reason=str(reason or ""),
    )

def dependents(self, molecule_id: int) -> dict[str, int]:
    """What hangs from this molecule's structure and would go if an edit replaced it."""
    from sqlalchemy import func, or_

    from amdockvs.models import DockingResultRecord
    from amdockvs.models.qsar import LigandActivity, QSARPrediction

    counts = {}
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        for label, model, clause in (
            ("activities", LigandActivity, LigandActivity.molecule_id == molecule_id),
            ("docking results", DockingResultRecord, or_(DockingResultRecord.ligand_molecule_id == molecule_id,

        ):
            counts[label] = int(session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(model).where(clause)).one())
    return {label: n for label, n in counts.items() if n}

copy=False replaces it: everything computed from the old structure goes (clear_derived: conformers, engine preparations, descriptors, fingerprints, docking results...) and so do its activities, measured on the old compound; the imported original (stored_payload_id), sets and complexes stay. copy=True leaves the molecule alone and adds the edit as a new one, with nothing of the old one's but its role. Source code in src/amdockvs/molecules/api.py 
def edit(self, molecule_id: int, molblock: str, *, copy: bool = False) -> int | None:
    """Give a molecule an edited structure (a molfile from the 2D editor).

    `copy=False` replaces it: everything computed from the old structure goes (`clear_derived`:
    conformers, engine preparations, descriptors, fingerprints, docking results...) and so do its
    activities, measured on the old compound; the imported original (stored_payload_id), sets and
    complexes stay. `copy=True` leaves the molecule alone and adds the edit as a new one, with
    nothing of the old one's but its role. Returns the id holding the edit, or None when the
    drawing is still the same compound, which changes nothing."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    from sqlalchemy import delete as sql_delete

    from amdockvs.chemistry.structures import molecule_mol, sdf_payload
    from amdockvs.core.payloads import payload_store
    from amdockvs.io.rows import identity_representations, structure_fields
    from amdockvs.models.qsar import LigandActivity
    from amdockvs.molecules.editing import edited_structure
    from amdockvs.project.deletion import clear_derived

    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    molecule = self.get(molecule_id)
    if molecule is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Molecule {molecule_id} does not exist.")
    mol = edited_structure(molblock, molecule_mol(project_db, molecule))
    if mol is None:
        return None
    fields = structure_fields(mol)
    identity = {key: fields.pop(key) for key in ("inchikey", "canonical_smiles")}
    store = payload_store(project_db)
    if not copy:
        clear_derived(project_db, [molecule.id])
    with project_db.get_session() as session:
        edited_payload, = store.put(session, [sdf_payload(mol)])
        if copy:
            parent = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(molecule.id))
            row = MoleculeRecord(**parent.model_dump(exclude={"id", "ro5_violations"}))
            row.name = f"{parent.name} (edited)"
            row.stored_payload_id = edited_payload  # the edit is all this molecule ever had
            row.in_set = False
            metadata = {"edited_from": int(parent.id)}
            replaced = None
        else:
            session.exec(sql_delete(LigandActivity).where(LigandActivity.molecule_id == int(molecule.id)))
            row = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(molecule.id))
            metadata = sanitize_molecule_extra_data(row.extra_data)
            for stale in ("chemistry", "history", "state"):  # described the structure that is gone
                metadata.pop(stale, None)
            replaced = row.current_payload_id
        row.current_payload_id = edited_payload
        for key, value in fields.items():
            setattr(row, key, value)
        row.is_minimized = False
        metadata["edited"] = True
        row.extra_data = metadata
        session.add(row)
        session.flush()
        for representation in identity_representations(identity, molecule_id=int(row.id)):
            session.merge(MoleculeRepresentation(**representation))
        session.commit()
        edited_id = int(row.id)
    if replaced:
        store.release([replaced])  # an earlier edit's bytes; the import is still referenced, so it stays
    return edited_id

def shard_counts(self, *, engine: str = "ad4") -> dict[str, int]:
    """Inventory of the sharded library: shards, molecules in them, and how many are prepared.

    Preparation is engine-specific and does not rewrite the chemical inventory.
    """
    from amdockvs.molecules.storage import ShardStore, iter_prepared_shards, shard_scope_spec

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    store = ShardStore(self.runtime.workspace.project_db)
    whole = shard_scope_spec()
    prepared = list(iter_prepared_shards(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, engine=engine))
    return {
        "shards": store.count(whole),
        "records": store.record_count(whole),
        "prepared": len(prepared),
        "prepared_records": sum(int(row.get("n_records") or 0) for row in prepared),
    }

def select_fragment(self, molecule_id: int, fragment_index: int) -> Any:
    """Make another component of the imported original the molecule's current structure.

    Fragments are not stored: this one is cut again from the original and written alone. What
    was computed from the old structure goes (`clear_derived`); activities, measured on the
    imported compound, stay."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    from amdockvs.chemistry.structures import molecule_mol, sdf_payload
    from amdockvs.core.payloads import payload_store
    from amdockvs.io.rows import identity_representations, structure_fields
    from amdockvs.molecules.fragments import fragments_of
    from amdockvs.project.deletion import clear_derived

    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    molecule = self.get(molecule_id)
    if molecule is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Molecule {molecule_id} does not exist.")
    original = molecule_mol(project_db, {"stored_payload_id": molecule.stored_payload_id})
    if original is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Molecule {molecule_id} has no imported original to take a fragment from.")
    fragment = fragments_of(original).get(int(fragment_index))
    if fragment is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Fragment {fragment_index} does not exist for molecule {molecule_id}.")
    store = payload_store(project_db)
    clear_derived(project_db, [molecule.id])
    with project_db.get_session() as session:
        fragment_payload, = store.put(session, [sdf_payload(fragment)])
        row = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(molecule.id))
        replaced = row.current_payload_id
        metadata = sanitize_molecule_extra_data(row.extra_data)
        if isinstance(metadata.get("fragmentation"), dict):  # a copy: in place, the JSON column sees no change
            metadata["fragmentation"] = {**metadata["fragmentation"], "selected_fragment_index": int(fragment_index)}
        for stale in ("chemistry", "history", "state"):  # described the structure that is gone
            metadata.pop(stale, None)
        row.extra_data = metadata
        row.current_payload_id = fragment_payload
        row.is_minimized = False
        fields = structure_fields(fragment)
        identity = {key: fields.pop(key) for key in ("inchikey", "canonical_smiles")}
        for key, value in fields.items():
            setattr(row, key, value)
        session.add(row)
        for representation in identity_representations(identity, molecule_id=int(row.id)):
            session.merge(MoleculeRepresentation(**representation))
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(row)
    if replaced:
        store.release([replaced])  # a no-op while it is still the import or a model's
    return row

def download(self, source, ids: Iterable[str], *, keep: bool = True, progress=None, cancel=None):
    """Fetch ``ids`` from a download ``source`` (a key of ``amdockvs.io.downloads.SOURCES``).
    ``keep=False`` puts them in the project's temporary downloads: the import that reads them
    deletes them once it has completed. Returns an ``Outcome`` (files, failures)."""
    from amdockvs.io import downloads

    source = downloads.SOURCES[source] if isinstance(source, str) else source
    folder = None if keep else downloads.temporary_folder(self.runtime.get_project_paths()["project_root"], source)
    return downloads.download(source, list(ids), folder=folder, progress=progress, cancel=cancel)

def shard_ligands(
    self,
    files: Iterable[PathLike],
    *,
    shard_size: int | None = None,
    executor_name: str = "compute",
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    molecule_kind: str = "small_molecule",
    prefilter: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    temporary_files: Iterable[PathLike] | None = None,
    force: bool = False,
) -> list[str]:
    """The `htpvs` import: split the library into shards, materialize nothing.

    Same feed as `load_ligands` — the byte-span splitter — with the record cap read as
    shard size. What changes is the worker: it writes the span back out as a file and
    registers a `screening_shards` row instead of parsing molecules into the project db.
    """
    normalized_files = normalize_files(files, label="ligand files")
    if not normalized_files:
        return []
    records = (
        default_shard_size(runtime=self.runtime)
        if shard_size is None
        else int(shard_size)
    )
    records = max(1, min(records, MAX_SHARD_RECORDS))
    params: dict[str, Any] = {
        "file_paths": [str(file_path) for file_path in normalized_files],
        **self._temporary(normalized_files, temporary_files),
        "batch_size": records,
        "molecule_kind": str(molecule_kind or "small_molecule"),
        **self._batches(normalized_files, force=force, kind=ImportKind.SHARDS, role="ligand"),
    }
    if prefilter:
        params["prefilter"] = dict(prefilter)
    return [
        self._submit_job(
            shard_ligands_job,
            params=params,
            executor_name=executor_name,
            depends_on=depends_on,
            # ramp=False, like the feed: an over-declared total never completes.
            total_chunks=_total_import_chunks(normalized_files, batch_size=records, ramp=False),
            max_inflight_tasks=import_max_inflight(self.runtime),
            # The queue that cuts the shards lives here, in the parent: it needs the
            # project's shard directory and its database, neither of which a job spec
            # knows at declaration time.
            result_handler_kwargs={
                "project_db": self.runtime.workspace.project_db,
                "shard_dir": self.runtime.get_project_resource_path(RESOURCE_SHARDS),
                "shard_size": records,
                "generation_id": self._import_generation_id(),
            },
        )
    ]

run_ligand_pipeline(["standardize", "protonate", "generate_3d"]) reads and writes every ligand once; the three single-step jobs read and rewrite the whole library three times.

With no explicit row scope, a sharded library dispatches whole shards automatically. Passing ligands always selects the row adapter for curated/reference molecules.

def run_ligand_pipeline(
    self,
    steps: Sequence[str | tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]],
    *,
    ligands: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    structure_source: str = "current",
    batch_size: int = 128,
    executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    wait: bool = False,
) -> str | JobStatus:
    """Run several chemistry steps in one pass over the active screening library.

    `run_ligand_pipeline(["standardize", "protonate", "generate_3d"])` reads and writes every
    ligand once; the three single-step jobs read and rewrite the whole library three times.

    With no explicit row scope, a sharded library dispatches whole shards automatically.
    Passing ``ligands`` always selects the row adapter for curated/reference molecules.

    ponytail: the single-step methods below validate their own arguments (pH range, method
    names, tool installs). Here the step params go through as given and the worker raises.
    """
    normalized = normalize_steps(steps)
    if not normalized:
        raise ValueError("run_ligand_pipeline needs at least one step.")
    for name, _params in normalized:
        if name not in LIGAND_STEPS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported ligand chemistry operation: {name}")
    normalized = [
        (name, self._protonate_params(**params) if name == "protonate" else params)
        for name, params in normalized
    ]
    if ligands is None:
        self.runtime._require_active_project()
        if has_shards(self.runtime.workspace.project_db):
            return self.run_shard_pipeline(
                normalized,
                executor_name=executor_name,
                depends_on=depends_on,
                wait=wait,
            )
    return self._submit_ligand_operation(
        [[name, params] for name, params in normalized],
        ligands=ligands,
        params={},
        structure_source=structure_source,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        wait=wait,
    )

def run_shard_pipeline(
    self,
    steps: Sequence[str | tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]],
    *,
    params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    wait: bool = False,
) -> str | JobStatus:
    """The same steps as `run_ligand_pipeline`, over the shards of an `htpvs` project.

    One shard per chunk, one file in and one file out. The run writes into a new
    generation and only switches to it if it finishes, so a crashed run changes nothing
    and the retry simply starts over from the generation that is still the library.
    """
    normalized = normalize_steps(steps)
    if not normalized:
        raise ValueError("run_shard_pipeline needs at least one step.")
    for name, _params in normalized:
        if name not in LIGAND_STEPS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported ligand chemistry operation: {name}")
    normalized = [
        (name, self._protonate_params(**params) if name == "protonate" else params)
        for name, params in normalized
    ]
    if any(name == "conformers" for name, _params in normalized):
        raise ValueError(
            "Sharded conformer ensembles are not supported: one shard record currently "
            "stores one molecular structure. Generate conformers after materialization."
        )
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    # Opened here, before anything runs: the feed needs its output directory and the
    # result handler needs its id, and neither can invent one of its own without the two
    # disagreeing about where the generation lives.
    label = "+".join(name for name, _ in normalized)
    shards_root = Path(self.runtime.get_project_resource_path(RESOURCE_SHARDS))
    generation_id = create_generation(project_db, step=label, shard_dir=shards_root)
    job_id = self.runtime.submit_job(
        shard_chemistry_job,
        params=ShardChemistryJobParams(
            operation=[[name, step_params] for name, step_params in normalized],
            params=dict(params or {}),
            generation_id=generation_id,
            output_dir=str(shards_root / f"gen_{generation_id:04d}_{label}"),
        ).model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        priority=SHARDS_PRIORITY,
        result_handler_kwargs={"project_db": project_db, "generation_id": generation_id},
    )
    return self.runtime.wait_for_job(job_id) if wait else job_id

def predict_receptors(
        self,
        *,
        receptors: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
        model: str = FAST_MODEL,
        force: bool = False,
        depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
        wait: bool = False,
) -> str | JobStatus:
    """Predict protein structures from sequence with the ESMFold API (thread executor).

    Only proteins without 3D by default; `force=True` predicts again and points the current structure
    to the new model. The token comes from ESM_API_KEY and is never stored.
    """
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    if not api_token():
        raise RuntimeError(f"{ESM_TOKEN_ENV} is not set: paste your Biohub API token first.")
    receptor_set_ref = None if receptors is None or is_molecule_scope(receptors) else ensure_molecule_set_ref(self.runtime, receptors, name="chemistry_receptor_predict_input")
    receptor_scope = scope_payload(receptors) if is_molecule_scope(receptors) else {}
    receptor_filters = dict(receptor_scope.get("filters") or {})
    if "molecule_type" not in receptor_filters:
        receptor_filters["is_receptor"] = True
    if receptor_scope.get("limit") is not None:
        receptor_filters["_limit"] = receptor_scope.get("limit")
    params = ReceptorPredictionJobParams(
        model=model,
        force=bool(force),
        receptor_set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        receptor_filters=receptor_filters if force else {**receptor_filters, "has_3d": False},
    )
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    total_items = db_count(project_db, prediction_scope_spec(params))
    # An empty scope with proteins in it means they all have 3D already. An empty scope with
    # no proteins at all may be an import still running: submit and let the job wait for it.
    if total_items == 0 and not force and db_count(project_db, prediction_scope_spec(params.model_copy(update={"receptor_filters": receptor_filters}))):
        raise ValueError("Every protein in scope already has a 3D structure; tick Force to predict again.")
    job_id = self.runtime.submit_job(
        receptor_prediction_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name="thread",
        depends_on=depends_on,
        total_chunks=total_items or None,
    )
    if wait:
        return self.runtime.wait_for_job(job_id)
    return job_id

def details(self, complex_ref: ComplexRef | int) -> Details | None:
    """Load the complete Details-panel projection for a receptor-ligand pair."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    complex_id = int(complex_ref.id if isinstance(complex_ref, ComplexRef) else complex_ref)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        pair = session.get(ComplexRecord, complex_id)
        if pair is None:
            return None
        receptor = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(pair.receptor_molecule_id or 0))
        ligand = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(pair.ligand_molecule_id or 0))
        activity = (
            session.get(LigandActivity, int(pair.activity_id or 0))
            if int(pair.activity_id or 0) > 0
            else None
        )
    return self.Details(complex=pair, receptor=receptor, ligand=ligand, activity=activity)

def compute_descriptors(
    self,
    *,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    only_missing: bool = True,
    batch_size: int = 1000,
    executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    compute_fingerprints: bool = False,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
    alerts: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Submit the descriptor job. only_missing=True skips ligands that already have
    descriptors computed (MoleculeRecord.mw populated). With compute_fingerprints=True it
    also stores a Morgan fingerprint per ligand, and only_missing then means "lacks that
    fingerprint" so FPs can be added to already-described ligands. With alerts=True it is
    the alerts job instead: PAINS and identity keys, which a library import leaves out."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    molecule_set_ref = (
        None
        if molecule_set is None or is_molecule_scope(molecule_set)
        else ensure_molecule_set_ref(self.runtime, molecule_set, name="qsar_descriptor_input")
    )
    molecule_scope = scope_payload(molecule_set) if is_molecule_scope(molecule_set) else {}
    filters = apply_workflow_filters(
        {**dict(molecule_scope.get("filters") or {}), "excluded": False},
        workflow=QSAR_WORKFLOW,
        role="ligand",
    )
    params = DescriptorJobParams(
        batch_size=batch_size,
        molecule_set_id=None if molecule_set_ref is None else int(molecule_set_ref.id),
        molecule_filters=filters,
        only_missing=bool(only_missing),
        compute_fingerprints=bool(compute_fingerprints),
        fp_radius=int(fp_radius),
        fp_nbits=int(fp_nbits),
        alerts=bool(alerts),
    )
    return self.runtime.submit_job(
        calculate_molecule_alerts_job if alerts else calculate_molecule_descriptors_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
    )

Per-ligand applicability domain by ECFP4 similarity: mean Tanimoto to the k nearest training ligands of model; in_domain = that mean >= threshold. Answers "is this prediction an interpolation or an extrapolation?". Needs Morgan fingerprints computed.

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def applicability_domain(
    self,
    *,
    model: QSARModelRef | int,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    k: int = 5,
    threshold: float = 0.3,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Per-ligand applicability domain by ECFP4 similarity: mean Tanimoto to the k nearest
    *training* ligands of ``model``; in_domain = that mean >= threshold. Answers "is this
    prediction an interpolation or an extrapolation?". Needs Morgan fingerprints computed."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    train_ids = [int(mid) for mid, sub in self.model_subsets(model=model).items() if sub == "train"]
    ligands = self._ligands(molecule_set)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        if not train_ids:  # model recorded no split → use every labeled training ligand as reference
            record = session.get(QSARModelRecord, int(model.id if hasattr(model, "id") else model))
            train_ids = [int(m) for m in ((record.metrics or {}).get("usable_ligands") or [])] if record else []
        fp_map = self._fingerprint_matrix(
            session, train_ids + [int(r.id or 0) for r in ligands], radius=fp_radius, nbits=fp_nbits
        )
        names = {int(r.id or 0): str(r.name or "") for r in ligands}
    train_fps = [fp_map[i] for i in train_ids if i in fp_map]
    if not train_fps:
        raise ValueError("No training fingerprints — compute Morgan fingerprints (ECFP4) first.")
    train_matrix = np.asarray(train_fps, dtype=float)
    train_norm = train_matrix.sum(axis=1)  # popcount per training fp
    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for rec in ligands:
        mid = int(rec.id or 0)
        query = fp_map.get(mid)
        if query is None:
            continue
        query = np.asarray(query, dtype=float)
        inter = train_matrix @ query  # |A ∩ B| per training fp
        union = train_norm + query.sum() - inter
        tanimoto = np.divide(inter, union, out=np.zeros_like(inter), where=union > 0)
        top = np.sort(tanimoto)[::-1][: max(1, int(k))]
        sim = float(np.mean(top))
        out.append({"molecule_id": mid, "name": names.get(mid, ""),
                    "similarity": sim, "in_domain": bool(sim >= float(threshold))})
    return out

Pearson correlation matrix across the descriptor block's features (over the project's ligands) — the redundancy the training pipeline prunes. feature_source 'descriptors' (14) or 'rdkit2d' (~200); ecfp4 is unsupported (2048 binary bits). Returns {labels, matrix, dropped} where dropped = features the |r|>corr_threshold filter would remove (kept feature listed first).

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def correlation_matrix(
    self,
    *,
    feature_source: str = "descriptors",
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    corr_threshold: float = 0.95,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Pearson correlation matrix across the descriptor block's features (over the project's
    ligands) — the redundancy the training pipeline prunes. feature_source 'descriptors' (14) or
    'rdkit2d' (~200); ecfp4 is unsupported (2048 binary bits). Returns {labels, matrix, dropped}
    where dropped = features the |r|>corr_threshold filter would remove (kept feature listed first)."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    source = str(feature_source).lower()
    if source in {"ecfp4", "fingerprint", "morgan"}:
        raise ValueError("Correlation heatmap is for descriptor blocks, not fingerprints.")
    if source in {"rdkit2d", "rdkit_2d", "rdkit-2d"}:
        feature_kind = "rdkit2d"
        from amdockvs.chemistry.descriptors import rdkit2d_descriptor_names

        features = tuple(rdkit2d_descriptor_names())
    else:
        feature_kind = "descriptors"
        features = normalize_feature_names(None)
    ligands = self._ligands(molecule_set)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        _ids, x_rows, names, _missing = self._design_matrix(
            session, ligands, feature_kind=feature_kind, features=features, fp_radius=2, fp_nbits=2048
        )
    if len(x_rows) < 2:
        raise ValueError("Need >=2 ligands with descriptors to compute correlations.")
    x_matrix = np.asarray(x_rows, dtype=float)
    # median-impute rdkit2d gaps, then drop zero-variance columns (correlation is undefined there)
    medians = np.nanmedian(x_matrix, axis=0)
    nan_idx = np.where(np.isnan(x_matrix))
    x_matrix[nan_idx] = np.take(medians, nan_idx[1])
    keep = x_matrix.var(axis=0) > 0
    x_matrix = x_matrix[:, keep]
    labels = [n for n, k in zip(names, keep) if k]
    corr = np.nan_to_num(np.corrcoef(x_matrix, rowvar=False), nan=0.0)
    from amdockvs.qsar.modeling import CorrelationFilter

    support = CorrelationFilter(threshold=float(corr_threshold)).fit(x_matrix).get_support()
    dropped = [n for n, kept in zip(labels, support) if not kept]
    return {"labels": labels, "matrix": corr.tolist(), "dropped": dropped, "n_ligands": int(x_matrix.shape[0])}

Scaffold split keeps whole scaffolds together but does NOT stratify by class, so an imbalanced endpoint can land most actives on one side. Returns {task, categories, train[], test[], n_train, n_test, note} — counts per class (classification) or per value-bin (regression), aligned to categories.

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def split_preview(
    self,
    *,
    endpoint: str,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    split: str = "scaffold",
    test_size: float = 0.3,
    class_threshold: float | None = None,
    seed: int = 0,
    bins: int = 10,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Train/test label distribution for an endpoint WITHOUT training, so you can see whether the
    split balances the labels — not just chemical space. Scaffold split keeps whole scaffolds
    together but does NOT stratify by class, so an imbalanced endpoint can land most actives on
    one side. Returns {task, categories, train[], test[], n_train, n_test, note} — counts per
    class (classification) or per value-bin (regression), aligned to `categories`."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    from amdockvs.qsar.modeling import grouped_holdout_split

    endpoint_text = str(endpoint or "").strip()
    if not endpoint_text:
        raise ValueError("split_preview requires endpoint.")
    ligands = self._ligands(molecule_set)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        activity_by_ligand = self._latest_activity_by_ligand(session, endpoint_text)
        labeled = [r for r in ligands if int(r.id or 0) in activity_by_ligand]
        used_ids = [int(r.id or 0) for r in labeled]
        scaffolds = self._scaffold_keys(labeled) if split == "scaffold" else {}
    if len(used_ids) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Only {len(used_ids)} labeled ligand(s) for '{endpoint_text}'.")
    y = np.asarray([activity_by_ligand[mid] for mid in used_ids], dtype=float)
    if split == "scaffold":
        train_idx, test_idx = grouped_holdout_split(
            [scaffolds.get(mid, "") for mid in used_ids], test_size=float(test_size), seed=int(seed)
        )
    else:
        from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

        train_idx, test_idx = train_test_split(
            list(range(len(used_ids))), test_size=float(test_size), random_state=int(seed)
        )
    kind = self.endpoint_kinds().get(endpoint_text, "")
    is_class = kind == "categorical" or class_threshold is not None or set(np.unique(y).tolist()) <= {0.0, 1.0}
    if is_class:
        yb = (y >= float(class_threshold)).astype(int) if class_threshold is not None else y.astype(int)
        classes = sorted(set(yb.tolist()))
        train = [int((yb[train_idx] == c).sum()) for c in classes]
        test = [int((yb[test_idx] == c).sum()) for c in classes]
        # active-class fraction on each side — the imbalance the split may distort
        pos = classes[-1] if classes else 1
        fr = lambda idx: float((yb[idx] == pos).mean()) if len(idx) else 0.0
        note = f"class {pos} fraction — train {fr(train_idx):.3f} vs test {fr(test_idx):.3f}"
        return {"task": "classification", "categories": [str(c) for c in classes],
                "train": train, "test": test, "n_train": len(train_idx), "n_test": len(test_idx), "note": note}
    lo, hi = float(y.min()), float(y.max())
    edges = np.linspace(lo, hi, int(bins) + 1) if hi > lo else np.array([lo, lo + 1.0])
    cats = [f"{edges[i]:.2g}" for i in range(len(edges) - 1)]
    train = [int(v) for v in np.histogram(y[train_idx], bins=edges)[0]]
    test = [int(v) for v in np.histogram(y[test_idx], bins=edges)[0]]
    note = f"mean value — train {float(y[train_idx].mean()):.3f} vs test {float(y[test_idx].mean()):.3f}"
    return {"task": "regression", "categories": cats, "train": train, "test": test,
            "n_train": len(train_idx), "n_test": len(test_idx), "note": note}

For descriptor sources the preprocessing (impute→drop zero-variance→drop |r|>corr_threshold→ scale) lives inside the CV pipeline, so scores are leakage-free. split 'scaffold' holds out whole Bemis-Murcko scaffolds. cv_folds>=2 adds a CV score (Q²/MCC). class_threshold binarizes a continuous endpoint (active = value >= threshold); leave None for categorical endpoints. y_scramble>=1 runs that many label-permutation refits (should score ~0; else signal is spurious).

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def train(
    self,
    *,
    endpoint: str,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    algorithm: str = "linear_regression",
    task: str = "regression",
    feature_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    feature_source: str = "descriptors",
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
    name: str = "",
    test_size: float = 0.0,
    split: str = "random",
    cv_folds: int = 0,
    class_threshold: float | None = None,
    corr_threshold: float = 0.95,
    y_scramble: int = 0,
    hyperparams: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> QSARModelRecord:
    """Fit a model template from the ligands of ``molecule_set`` that have an activity for
    ``endpoint``. feature_source: 'descriptors' (14 physchem columns), 'rdkit2d' (full ~200
    RDKit block, computed+cached on first use) or 'ecfp4' (stored Morgan fingerprint). For
    descriptor sources the preprocessing (impute→drop zero-variance→drop |r|>corr_threshold→
    scale) lives inside the CV pipeline, so scores are leakage-free. split 'scaffold' holds out
    whole Bemis-Murcko scaffolds. cv_folds>=2 adds a CV score (Q²/MCC). class_threshold binarizes
    a *continuous* endpoint (active = value >= threshold); leave None for categorical endpoints.
    y_scramble>=1 runs that many label-permutation refits (should score ~0; else signal is spurious)."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    endpoint_text = str(endpoint or "").strip()
    if not endpoint_text:
        raise ValueError("train requires endpoint.")
    source = str(feature_source).lower()
    if source in {"ecfp4", "fingerprint", "morgan"}:
        feature_kind = "ecfp4"
    elif source in {"rdkit2d", "rdkit_2d", "rdkit-2d"}:
        feature_kind = "rdkit2d"
    else:
        feature_kind = "descriptors"
    if feature_kind == "descriptors":
        features = normalize_feature_names(feature_names)
    elif feature_kind == "rdkit2d":
        from amdockvs.chemistry.descriptors import rdkit2d_descriptor_names

        features = tuple(rdkit2d_descriptor_names())
    else:
        features = ()
    ligands = self._ligands(molecule_set)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        activity_by_ligand = self._latest_activity_by_ligand(session, endpoint_text)
        labeled = [r for r in ligands if int(r.id or 0) in activity_by_ligand]
        missing_act = len(ligands) - len(labeled)
        used_ids, x_rows, out_names, missing_desc = self._design_matrix(
            session, labeled, feature_kind=feature_kind, features=features, fp_radius=fp_radius, fp_nbits=fp_nbits
        )
        scaffolds = self._scaffold_keys(labeled) if split == "scaffold" else {}
    y_rows = [activity_by_ligand[mid] for mid in used_ids]
    if len(x_rows) < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"train needs >=2 usable ligands; got {len(x_rows)} "
            f"(missing_descriptor={missing_desc}, missing_activity={missing_act})."
        )

    x_matrix = np.asarray(x_rows, dtype=float)
    y_raw = np.asarray(y_rows, dtype=float)
    if task == "classification":
        y_vector = (y_raw >= float(class_threshold)).astype(int) if class_threshold is not None else y_raw.astype(int)
    else:
        y_vector = y_raw

    if task == "classification" and np.unique(y_vector).size < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            "All ligands fall in a single class after labeling — a model can't be trained. "
            "For a categorical endpoint don't set a class threshold (the value is already the "
            "label); for a continuous one, pick a threshold that leaves both classes populated."
        )

    x_train, y_train, holdout = x_matrix, y_vector, None
    test_ids: set[int] = set()  # for split-membership reporting (train/test; no separate val set)
    if test_size and 0.0 < float(test_size) < 1.0 and x_matrix.shape[0] >= 4:
        if split == "scaffold":
            from amdockvs.qsar.modeling import grouped_holdout_split

            train_idx, test_idx = grouped_holdout_split(
                [scaffolds.get(mid, "") for mid in used_ids], test_size=float(test_size), seed=int(seed)
            )
            if test_idx and train_idx:
                x_train, y_train = x_matrix[train_idx], y_vector[train_idx]
                holdout = (x_matrix[test_idx], y_vector[test_idx])
                test_ids = {used_ids[i] for i in test_idx}
        else:
            from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

            indices = np.arange(x_matrix.shape[0])
            train_i, test_i = train_test_split(indices, test_size=float(test_size), random_state=int(seed))
            x_train, y_train = x_matrix[train_i], y_vector[train_i]
            holdout = (x_matrix[test_i], y_vector[test_i])
            test_ids = {used_ids[i] for i in test_i}

    fitted = fit_model(
        x_train, y_train, feature_names=out_names, algorithm=algorithm, task=task, hyperparams=hyperparams,
        feature_kind=feature_kind, corr_threshold=float(corr_threshold),
        fp_radius=fp_radius if feature_kind == "ecfp4" else None,
        fp_nbits=fp_nbits if feature_kind == "ecfp4" else None,
    )
    feature_summary = {
        "descriptors": list(out_names),
        "rdkit2d": f"rdkit2d:{len(out_names)}",
        "ecfp4": f"ecfp4:{fp_nbits}",
    }[feature_kind]
    metrics: dict[str, Any] = {
        "task": task,
        "algorithm": algorithm,
        "feature_kind": feature_kind,
        "features": feature_summary,
        "split": split,
        "class_threshold": class_threshold,
        "corr_threshold": float(corr_threshold),
        "n_train": int(x_train.shape[0]),
        "train": self._score(task, y_train, fitted, x_train),
        "usable_ligands": used_ids,
        "split_assignment": [[mid, "test" if mid in test_ids else "train"] for mid in used_ids],
    }
    if holdout is not None:
        metrics["test"] = self._score(task, holdout[1], fitted, holdout[0])
    if cv_folds and int(cv_folds) >= 2:
        from amdockvs.qsar.modeling import cross_val_score_mean

        metrics["cv_folds"] = int(cv_folds)
        cv_score = cross_val_score_mean(
            x_matrix, y_vector, algorithm=algorithm, task=task, cv=int(cv_folds),
            hyperparams=hyperparams, feature_kind=feature_kind, corr_threshold=float(corr_threshold),
        )
        metrics["q2" if task == "regression" else "cv_mcc"] = cv_score
    if y_scramble and int(y_scramble) >= 1:
        from amdockvs.qsar.modeling import y_scramble_score

        metrics["y_scramble"] = y_scramble_score(
            x_matrix, y_vector, algorithm=algorithm, task=task, n_permutations=int(y_scramble),
            hyperparams=hyperparams, feature_kind=feature_kind, corr_threshold=float(corr_threshold), seed=int(seed),
        )
    importance = feature_importance(fitted.estimator, out_names)
    if importance:
        metrics["feature_importance"] = [[n, v] for n, v in importance]

    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        model_record = QSARModelRecord(
            name=str(name or "").strip() or f"{algorithm}_{endpoint_text}",
            algorithm=algorithm,
            target=endpoint_text,
            feature_type="descriptors_2d",
            source="trained",
            metrics=metrics,
        )
        session.add(model_record)
        session.flush()
        session.refresh(model_record)
        artifact = self._artifact_path(f"model_{int(model_record.id or 0)}.joblib")
        save_model(artifact, fitted)
        model_record.model_path = str(artifact.relative_to(self._project_root()))
        session.add(model_record)
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(model_record)
        return model_record

items.text:
roc_curve_points(*, model: QSARModelRef | int, molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None, endpoint: str | None = None, subset: str = 'all') -> dict[str, Any]

(fpr, tpr) ROC points + AUC for a binary classification model. subset 'test' (held-out — the honest predictivity), 'train' (optimistic; the gap to test shows overfitting) or 'all'. Classification-only; needs a probabilistic model and both classes present.

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def roc_curve_points(
    self,
    *,
    model: QSARModelRef | int,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    endpoint: str | None = None,
    subset: str = "all",
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """(fpr, tpr) ROC points + AUC for a binary classification model. subset 'test' (held-out —
    the honest predictivity), 'train' (optimistic; the gap to test shows overfitting) or 'all'.
    Classification-only; needs a probabilistic model and both classes present."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    ligands = self._ligands(molecule_set)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        record, fitted = self._load_fitted(session, model)
        if fitted.task != "classification":
            raise ValueError("ROC curve is only for classification models.")
        endpoint_text = str(endpoint or record.target or "").strip()
        activity_by_ligand = self._latest_activity_by_ligand(session, endpoint_text)
        threshold = (record.metrics or {}).get("class_threshold")
        labeled = [r for r in ligands if int(r.id or 0) in activity_by_ligand]
        labeled = self._filter_by_subset(labeled, record, subset)
        used_ids, x_rows, _n, _m = self._design_matrix(
            session, labeled, feature_kind=fitted.feature_kind, features=self._features_for(fitted),
            fp_radius=int(fitted.fp_radius or 2), fp_nbits=int(fitted.fp_nbits or 2048),
        )
    if not x_rows:
        raise ValueError(f"No labeled, feature-complete ligands in the '{subset}' subset for a ROC curve.")
    x_matrix = np.asarray(x_rows, dtype=float)
    y_raw = np.asarray([activity_by_ligand[mid] for mid in used_ids], dtype=float)
    y_true = (y_raw >= float(threshold)).astype(int) if threshold is not None else y_raw.astype(int)
    # A stale/0.0 threshold on a categorical 0/1 endpoint collapses every label to one class —
    # fall back to the raw labels (the endpoint is already categorical) so old models still plot.
    if threshold is not None and len(set(y_true.tolist())) != 2:
        y_true = y_raw.astype(int)
    estimator = fitted.estimator
    if not hasattr(estimator, "predict_proba") or len(set(y_true.tolist())) != 2:
        raise ValueError("ROC needs a probabilistic binary model with both classes labeled.")
    from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, roc_curve

    proba = np.asarray(estimator.predict_proba(x_matrix))
    if proba.ndim != 2 or proba.shape[1] < 2:
        raise ValueError("model was trained on a single class — retrain it (no ROC possible).")
    scores = proba[:, 1]
    fpr, tpr, _thr = roc_curve(y_true, scores)
    return {
        "endpoint": endpoint_text,
        "subset": str(subset or "all").lower(),
        "points": [(float(a), float(b)) for a, b in zip(fpr, tpr)],
        "auc": float(roc_auc_score(y_true, scores)),
        "n": int(len(y_true)),
    }

def predict_shards(
    self,
    *,
    model: QSARModelRef | int,
    executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """``predict`` over the library's shards, as a job at ``SHARDS_PRIORITY``. Every shard
    is scored into a file of its own, keyed by ``io.shards.shard_key``; nothing enters the
    database until ``promote_shard_predictions`` cuts it. Scoring again overwrites each
    shard's file. Returns the job id."""

    model_id = int(model.id if hasattr(model, "id") else model)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        record = session.get(QSARModelRecord, model_id)

            raise ValueError(f"Unknown QSAR model id: {model_id}")
    params = ShardPredictJobParams(
        model_path=str(self._project_root() / record.model_path),
        output_dir=str(self._shard_predictions_dir(model_id)),
    )
    return self.runtime.submit_job(
        predict_shards_job, params=params.model_dump(mode="python"), executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on, priority=SHARDS_PRIORITY,
    )

A model's predictions over the library's shards, as a frame (key, value, confidence). Only the active generation's shards are read: an older one is no longer the library.

ponytail: the whole frame in RAM (~24 B/molecule, 2.4 GB at 10^8); a per-file top-N before the concat when a library gets there.

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def shard_predictions(self, *, model: QSARModelRef | int):
    """A model's predictions over the library's shards, as a frame (key, value, confidence).
    Only the active generation's shards are read: an older one is no longer the library.

    ponytail: the whole frame in RAM (~24 B/molecule, 2.4 GB at 10^8); a per-file top-N
    before the concat when a library gets there."""
    import pandas as pd

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    directory = self._shard_predictions_dir(int(model.id if hasattr(model, "id") else model))
    paths = [directory / f"{int(row['id'])}.parquet"
             for row in ShardStore(self.runtime.workspace.project_db).iter_rows(batch_size=1000)]
    frames = [pd.read_parquet(path) for path in paths if path.is_file()]
    if not frames:
        return pd.DataFrame({"key": pd.Series(dtype="int64"), "value": pd.Series(dtype=float),
                             "confidence": pd.Series(dtype=float)})
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)

items.title: promote_shard_predictions
items.text:
promote_shard_predictions(*, model: QSARModelRef | int, top_n: int | None = None, cutoff: float | None = None, higher_is_better: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]

The cut of cut_predictions over the library's predictions: the records kept become molecule rows carrying their prediction, so everything that reads rows (the Predictions view, cut_predictions, docking) has them. Ties break by key. Returns {"scored": n, "kept": n, "molecule_ids": the kept, best first}.

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def promote_shard_predictions(
    self,
    *,
    model: QSARModelRef | int,
    top_n: int | None = None,
    cutoff: float | None = None,
    higher_is_better: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The cut of ``cut_predictions`` over the library's predictions: the records kept become
    molecule rows carrying their prediction, so everything that reads rows (the Predictions
    view, ``cut_predictions``, docking) has them. Ties break by key. Returns {"scored": n,
    "kept": n, "molecule_ids": the kept, best first}."""
    if top_n is None and cutoff is None:
        raise ValueError("promote_shard_predictions needs top_n and/or cutoff.")
    model_id = int(model.id if hasattr(model, "id") else model)
    frame = self.shard_predictions(model=model_id)
    scored = len(frame)
    if cutoff is not None:
        frame = frame[frame["value"] >= float(cutoff) if higher_is_better else frame["value"] <= float(cutoff)]
    frame = frame.sort_values(["value", "key"], ascending=[not higher_is_better, True])
    if top_n is not None:
        frame = frame.head(max(0, int(top_n)))
    kept = [(int(key), float(value), confidence) for key, value, confidence in frame.itertuples(index=False)]
    promoted = ShardStore(self.runtime.workspace.project_db).promote(key for key, _value, _conf in kept)
    ids = [promoted[key] for key, _value, _conf in kept if key in promoted]
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        for start in range(0, len(ids), 900):
            for row in session.exec(
                select(QSARPredictionRecord)
                .where(QSARPredictionRecord.model_id == model_id)
                .where(QSARPredictionRecord.molecule_id.in_(ids[start:start + 900]))
            ).all():
                session.delete(row)
        session.flush()
        session.add_all(
            QSARPredictionRecord(
                molecule_id=promoted[key], model_id=model_id, value=value,
                confidence=None if confidence != confidence else float(confidence),  # NaN = none
            )
            for key, value, confidence in kept if key in promoted
        )
        session.commit()
    return {"scored": scored, "kept": len(ids), "molecule_ids": ids}
