def prediction_rows(self, *, model: QSARModelRef | int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Predictions joined with the ligand name, for the Predictions table:
    [{molecule_id, name, value, confidence}] ordered by ligand id. Excluded ligands are left
    out, as in every other ligand listing."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    model_id = int(model.id if hasattr(model, "id") else model)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        rows = list(session.exec(
            select(QSARPredictionRecord)
            .where(QSARPredictionRecord.model_id == model_id)
            .order_by(QSARPredictionRecord.molecule_id)
        ))
        names = {
            int(m.id): str(m.name or "")
            for m in session.exec(
                select(MoleculeRecord)
                .where(MoleculeRecord.id.in_([int(r.molecule_id) for r in rows] or [0]))
                .where(MoleculeRecord.excluded == False)  # noqa: E712
            )
        }
    return [
        {"molecule_id": int(r.molecule_id), "name": names[int(r.molecule_id)],
         "value": float(r.value), "confidence": None if r.confidence is None else float(r.confidence)}
        for r in rows if int(r.molecule_id) in names
    ]

items.title: cut_predictions
items.text:
cut_predictions(*, model: QSARModelRef | int, top_n: int | None = None, cutoff: float | None = None, higher_is_better: bool = True, exclude_rest: bool = False, ids_limit: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]

Use a model's predictions as a filter: keep the ligands at or beyond cutoff (>= when higher is better, <= otherwise) and, of those, at most the top_n best (ties break by id). With exclude_rest every other ligand the model scored is marked excluded (reversible); ligands it could not score, and ligands already excluded, are left alone.

The cut is a subquery over the predictions, so nothing here grows with the library: the exclusion is one UPDATE and only ids_limit ids ever come back. Returns {"kept": n, "rest": n, "excluded": how many were marked, "ids": the first ids_limit kept, best first}.

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def cut_predictions(
    self,
    *,
    model: QSARModelRef | int,
    top_n: int | None = None,
    cutoff: float | None = None,
    higher_is_better: bool = True,
    exclude_rest: bool = False,
    ids_limit: int = 0,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Use a model's predictions as a filter: keep the ligands at or beyond ``cutoff`` (>= when
    higher is better, <= otherwise) and, of those, at most the ``top_n`` best (ties break by
    id). With ``exclude_rest`` every other ligand the model scored is marked excluded
    (reversible); ligands it could not score, and ligands already excluded, are left alone.

    The cut is a subquery over the predictions, so nothing here grows with the library: the
    exclusion is one UPDATE and only ``ids_limit`` ids ever come back. Returns {"kept": n,
    "rest": n, "excluded": how many were marked, "ids": the first ``ids_limit`` kept, best first}."""
    if top_n is None and cutoff is None:
        raise ValueError("cut_predictions needs top_n and/or cutoff.")
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    model_id = int(model.id if hasattr(model, "id") else model)
    scored_ligand = aliased(MoleculeRecord)  # aliased: the UPDATE below targets the table itself
    scored = (
        select(QSARPredictionRecord.molecule_id)
        .join(scored_ligand, scored_ligand.id == QSARPredictionRecord.molecule_id)
        .where(QSARPredictionRecord.model_id == model_id, scored_ligand.excluded == False)  # noqa: E712
    )
    value = QSARPredictionRecord.value
    kept = scored.order_by(value.desc() if higher_is_better else value.asc(), QSARPredictionRecord.molecule_id)
    if cutoff is not None:
        kept = kept.where(value >= float(cutoff) if higher_is_better else value <= float(cutoff))
    if top_n is not None:
        kept = kept.limit(max(0, int(top_n)))
    how = (f"top {int(top_n)}" if top_n is not None else "") + (
        f"{' ' if top_n is not None else ''}{'>=' if higher_is_better else '<='} {float(cutoff):g}"
        if cutoff is not None else "")
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        n_scored = int(session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(scored.subquery())).one())
        n_kept = int(session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(kept.subquery())).one())
        ids = [int(i) for i in session.exec(kept.limit(min(int(ids_limit), n_kept)))] if ids_limit else []
        excluded = 0
        if exclude_rest and n_kept < n_scored:
            result = session.exec(
                sql_update(MoleculeRecord)
                .where(MoleculeRecord.id.in_(scored), MoleculeRecord.id.not_in(kept))
                .values(excluded=True, exclusion_reason=f"qsar: outside the cut of model #{model_id} ({how})")
            )
            excluded = int(getattr(result, "rowcount", 0) or 0)
            session.commit()
    return {"kept": n_kept, "rest": n_scored - n_kept, "excluded": excluded, "ids": ids}

Score a labeled molecule set against a model and return task-appropriate metrics.

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def evaluate(
    self,
    *,
    model: QSARModelRef | int,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    endpoint: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score a labeled molecule set against a model and return task-appropriate metrics."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    ligands = self._ligands(molecule_set)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        record, fitted = self._load_fitted(session, model)
        endpoint_text = str(endpoint or record.target or "").strip()
        if not endpoint_text:
            raise ValueError("evaluate needs an endpoint (model has no target).")
        activity_by_ligand = self._latest_activity_by_ligand(session, endpoint_text)
        features = self._features_for(fitted)
        threshold = (record.metrics or {}).get("class_threshold")
        labeled = [r for r in ligands if int(r.id or 0) in activity_by_ligand]
        used_ids, x_rows, _names, _missing = self._design_matrix(
            session, labeled, feature_kind=fitted.feature_kind, features=features,
            fp_radius=int(fitted.fp_radius or 2), fp_nbits=int(fitted.fp_nbits or 2048),
        )
        if not x_rows:
            raise ValueError("No labeled, descriptor-complete ligands to evaluate.")
        x_matrix = np.asarray(x_rows, dtype=float)
        y_raw = np.asarray([activity_by_ligand[mid] for mid in used_ids], dtype=float)
        if fitted.task == "classification":
            y_eval = (y_raw >= float(threshold)).astype(int) if threshold is not None else y_raw.astype(int)
            metrics = self._score("classification", y_eval, fitted, x_matrix)
        else:
            metrics = self._score("regression", y_raw, fitted, x_matrix)
        metrics["model_id"] = int(record.id or 0)
        metrics["endpoint"] = endpoint_text
        return metrics

atom_contributions(*, model: QSARModelRef | int, ligand_id: int) -> dict[str, Any]

Per-atom contribution to an ECFP4 model's prediction (StarDrop's "glowing molecule"). Returns {molblock, weights[per atom], prediction}. ECFP4 models only.

Source code in src/amdockvs/qsar/api.py 
def atom_contributions(self, *, model: QSARModelRef | int, ligand_id: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Per-atom contribution to an ECFP4 model's prediction (StarDrop's "glowing molecule").
    Returns {molblock, weights[per atom], prediction}. ECFP4 models only."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    from rdkit import Chem, DataStructs
    from rdkit.Chem.Draw import SimilarityMaps

    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        record, fitted = self._load_fitted(session, model)
        if fitted.feature_kind != "ecfp4":
            raise ValueError("Glowing molecule needs an ECFP4 (fingerprint) model.")
        rec = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(ligand_id))
        if rec is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown ligand id: {ligand_id}")
        mol = self._ligand_mol(session, rec)
    if mol is None:
        raise ValueError("No structure available for this ligand.")
    radius, nbits = int(fitted.fp_radius or 2), int(fitted.fp_nbits or 2048)

    def fp_fn(probe, atom_id=-1):
        return SimilarityMaps.GetMorganFingerprint(probe, atomId=atom_id, radius=radius, nBits=nbits)

    # A classifier's label does not move when one atom is removed, so every weight would be
    # 0: follow the probability instead — P(active) when binary, else P(predicted class).
    proba = getattr(fitted.estimator, "predict_proba", None) if fitted.task == "classification" else None
    column = -1

    def row(fp):
        arr = np.zeros((nbits,), dtype=np.float64)
        DataStructs.ConvertToNumpyArray(fp, arr)
        return arr.reshape(1, -1)

    def pred_fn(fp):
        if proba is None:
            return float(fitted.predict(row(fp))[0])
        return float(proba(row(fp))[0][column])

    if proba is not None and len(fitted.classes) > 2:
        column = int(np.argmax(proba(row(fp_fn(mol)))[0]))
    weights = SimilarityMaps.GetAtomicWeightsForModel(mol, fp_fn, pred_fn)
    return {
        "molblock": Chem.MolToMolBlock(mol),
        "weights": [float(w) for w in weights],
        "prediction": pred_fn(fp_fn(mol)),
    }

Saves a site. Without binding_site_id it creates a new one; with it, rewrites that one.

Source code in src/amdockvs/binding_sites/api.py 
def save_site(
        self,
        *,
        molecule_id: int,
        name: str = "",
        source: str = "manual",
        source_ref: str = "",
        center: tuple[float, float, float],
        size: tuple[float, float, float],
        binding_site_id: int | None = None,
        set_active: bool = False,
        extra_data: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> BindingSite:
    """Saves a site. Without `binding_site_id` it creates a new one; with it, rewrites that one."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        molecule = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(molecule_id))
        if molecule is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Molecule {molecule_id} does not exist.")
        site = None if binding_site_id is None else session.get(BindingSite, int(binding_site_id))
        if site is None:
            site = BindingSite(molecule_id=int(molecule_id))
        elif int(site.molecule_id) != int(molecule_id):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Binding site {binding_site_id} belongs to molecule {site.molecule_id}."
            )
        site.name = str(name or "")
        site.source = str(source or "manual")
        site.source_ref = str(source_ref or "")
        site.center_x = float(center[0])
        site.center_y = float(center[1])
        site.center_z = float(center[2])
        site.size_x = float(size[0])
        site.size_y = float(size[1])
        site.size_z = float(size[2])
        site.extra_data = dict(extra_data or {})
        session.add(site)
        session.flush()
        if set_active:
            set_active_site_row(session, int(molecule_id), int(site.id))
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(site)
        return site

def suggest_box_from_ligand(
        self,
        *,
        ligand_id: int,
        scale: float | None = None,
        padding: float | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Auto box from a reference ligand: center = its centroid, size = cubic box
    derived from the ligand's radius of gyration. Returns {center, size, rg}.

    `scale`/`padding` default to the configured geometry (settings > binding_sites)."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        ligand = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(ligand_id))
        if ligand is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Molecule {ligand_id} does not exist.")
        payload_id = molecule_payload_id(ligand)
    if payload_id is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Ligand {ligand_id} has no stored structure.")
    coords = _read_atom_coords(*read_structure(self.runtime, payload_id))
    if not coords:
        raise ValueError(f"No atom coordinates found in ligand {ligand_id}.")
    geometry = app_config(self.runtime).binding_sites
    return box_from_coords(
        coords,
        scale=geometry.box_scale if scale is None else float(scale),
        padding=geometry.box_padding if padding is None else float(padding),
        minimum=geometry.box_min_edge,
        maximum=geometry.box_max_edge,
    )

def check_protocol(
    self, *, program: str, engine_config: dict, protocol_metadata: dict | None = None,

    """Check the program's current configuration without deleting or submitting anything."""

Return total/ready/failed preparation counts for a molecule scope.

Source code in src/amdockvs/docking/api.py 
def preparation_summary(
        self,
        scope: MoleculeScope,
        *,
        role_type: str,
        engine: str = "ad4",
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Return total/ready/failed preparation counts for a molecule scope."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    normalized_role = str(role_type or "").strip().lower()
    normalized_engine = str(engine or "ad4").strip().lower()
    if normalized_role not in {"ligand", "receptor"}:
        raise ValueError("role_type must be 'ligand' or 'receptor'.")
    # Count each side alone first: a family with no state row of that kind anywhere needs
    # no join with the scope (the common case before the first preparation).
    molecules = self.runtime.molecules
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    flags = {"is_ligand" if normalized_role == "ligand" else "is_receptor": True, "prepared_engine_key": normalized_engine}

    def in_scope(ready: bool) -> int:
        states = prepared_molecules_spec(role_type=normalized_role, engine=normalized_engine, is_ready=ready)
        if not db_count(project_db, states):
            return 0
        return molecules.count(molecules.filter(scope, filters={**flags, "prepared": ready}))

    total = molecules.count(scope)
    return {"total": total, "ready": in_scope(True) if total else 0, "failed": in_scope(False) if total else 0}

Opaque SmartTable clause selecting molecules not ready for every engine family.

Source code in src/amdockvs/docking/api.py 
def unprepared_molecules_clause(self, *, role_type: str, engines: list[str] | tuple[str, ...]):
    """Opaque SmartTable clause selecting molecules not ready for every engine family."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    role = str(role_type or "").strip().lower()
    if role not in {"ligand", "receptor"}:
        raise ValueError("role_type must be 'ligand' or 'receptor'.")
    normalized_engines = tuple(
        dict.fromkeys(str(value or "").strip().lower() for value in engines if str(value or "").strip()))
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    if any(
        not db_count(project_db, prepared_molecules_spec(role_type=role, engine=engine))
        for engine in normalized_engines
    ):
        return None  # a family nothing is ready for leaves every row in: no anti-join to run
    # NOT IN, not a correlated NOT EXISTS: DuckDB (1 thread, 1 GB) hash-joins the whole
    # table for the latter (4 s and GBs of spill for one page); SQLite is faster with it too.
    model, molecule_column, payload_column = prep_table(role)
    missing = [
        MoleculeRecord.id.not_in(
            select(molecule_column).where(model.family == engine, payload_column.is_not(None))
        )
        for engine in normalized_engines
    ]
    if not missing:
        return None
    return missing[0] if len(missing) == 1 else or_(*missing)

        *,
        program: str = VINA_PROGRAM.key,

No ligand scope — the library is the inventory of prepared shards. When the run ends, the best hit_cap ligands per receptor that pass the hit_threshold prefilter become rows; both are required, not defaulted: a campaign without them writes back everything it scored, which is the failure mode htpvs exists to prevent. A dependent off-target stage sets selected_from_receptor_id; its deferred chunker reads that receptor's durable Top-N and extracts only those records from the source shards.

Source code in src/amdockvs/docking/api.py 
def run_shards(
        self,
        *,
        program: str = VINA_PROGRAM.key,
        receptor_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
        hit_threshold: float,
        hit_cap: int,
        output_dir: PathLike | None = None,
        exhaustiveness: int = 8,
        num_modes: int = 9,
        box_center: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
        box_size: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
        scoring_function: str = "vina",
        vina_backend: str = DEFAULT_VINA_BACKEND,
        vina_command: str = DEFAULT_VINA_COMMAND,
        vina_cpu: int = 1,
        seed: int = 0,
        spacing: float = 0.375,
        energy_range: float = 3.0,
        min_rmsd: float = 1.0,
        run_id: str | None = None,
        protocol_metadata: dict | None = None,
        engine_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
        depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
        skip_existing: bool = True,
        payload: str = PAYLOAD_LIGHT,
        check_required: bool = True,
        selected_from_receptor_id: int | None = None,
        selected_top_n: int | None = None,
        replace_existing: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """`run` for a sharded library: the campaign, with the gate that makes it end.

    No ligand scope — the library is the inventory of prepared shards. When the run ends, the
    best `hit_cap` ligands per receptor that pass the `hit_threshold` prefilter become rows;
    both are required, not defaulted: a campaign without them writes back everything it
    scored, which is the failure mode `htpvs` exists to prevent. A dependent off-target
    stage sets `selected_from_receptor_id`; its deferred chunker reads that receptor's
    durable Top-N and extracts only those records from the source shards.
    """
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    if selected_top_n is not None and selected_from_receptor_id is None:
        raise ValueError("selected_top_n requires selected_from_receptor_id.")
    if selected_from_receptor_id is not None and not str(run_id or "").strip():
        raise ValueError("Off-target selection requires the reference run_id.")
    if (box_center is None) ^ (box_size is None):
        raise ValueError("docking.run requires both box_center and box_size when either one is provided.")
    program_spec = self.get_program_spec(program)
    if not program_spec.supports_shards:
        raise ValueError(f"Docking program '{program_spec.key}' does not support sharded libraries.")
    knobs = dict(
        exhaustiveness=exhaustiveness,
        num_modes=num_modes,
        scoring_function=scoring_function,
        vina_backend=vina_backend,
        vina_command=vina_command,
        vina_cpu=vina_cpu,
        seed=seed,
        spacing=spacing,
        energy_range=energy_range,
        min_rmsd=min_rmsd,
    )
    resolved_engine_config = _validated_engine_config(program_spec, engine_config, **knobs)
    protocol_metadata = self.check_protocol(
        program=program_spec.key, engine_config=resolved_engine_config,
        protocol_metadata=protocol_metadata, replace_existing=replace_existing,
    )
    reset_results = replace_existing and check_protocol_conflict(
        self.runtime.workspace.project_db, program=program_spec, protocol=protocol_metadata, replace_existing=True,
    )
    if reset_results and selected_from_receptor_id is not None:
        raise ValueError("Changing docking configuration requires rerunning the reference stage before off-target docking.")
    receptor_set_ref = self._set_ref(receptor_set, name="docking_receptor_input")
    receptor_scope = scope_payload(receptor_set) if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else {}
    receptor_filters = self._program_scope_filters(receptor_scope, role="receptor", program=program_spec)
    params = DockShardsJobParams(
        output_dir=self._output_dir(output_dir),
        engine=program_spec.docking_engine,
        preparation_engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        receptor_set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        receptor_filters=receptor_filters,
        box_center=box_center,
        box_size=box_size,
        **_engine_fields(resolved_engine_config, knobs),
        run_id=str(run_id or uuid4().hex),
        protocol_metadata=DockingProtocolMetadata.from_mapping(protocol_metadata or {}),
        engine_config=resolved_engine_config,
        hit_threshold=float(hit_threshold),
        hit_cap=int(hit_cap),
        selected_from_receptor_id=selected_from_receptor_id,
        selected_top_n=(int(selected_top_n) if selected_top_n is not None else int(hit_cap)),
        skip_existing=skip_existing,
        check_required=check_required,
    )
    if reset_results:
        if check_required and not depends_on:
            dock_shards_job.count_chunks(
                params.model_dump(mode="python"), config={"project_db": self.runtime.workspace.project_db},
            )
        clear_previous_docking(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, program=program_spec)
    return self.runtime.submit_job(
        dock_shards_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        priority=SHARDS_PRIORITY,
        cpu_required=program_spec.resource_requirements(resolved_engine_config)["cpu_required"],
        # The gate lives in the parent, like the shard queue at import: it counts across
        # chunks and it writes molecules, neither of which a worker can do.
        result_handler_kwargs={
            "project_db": self.runtime.workspace.project_db,
            "hit_cap": int(hit_cap),
            "hit_threshold": float(hit_threshold),
            "run_id": params.run_id,
            "engine": params.engine,
            "protocol_hash": str(params.protocol_metadata.hash or ""),
            "payload": str(payload),
            "selected_from_receptor_id": params.selected_from_receptor_id,
        },
    )

def method_misfit_receptor_ids(self, *, method: str) -> list[int]:
    """Receptors whose active box does not fit the docking `method` (methods.py).
    Receptors without a box are not judged: the user still has to define one. The source
    structure is read: preparation keeps its metals."""
    from amdockvs.docking.methods import excludes

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        rows = session.exec(
            select(MoleculeRecord, BindingSite)
            .join(BindingSite, (BindingSite.molecule_id == MoleculeRecord.id) & (BindingSite.is_active == True))  # noqa: E712
            .where(MoleculeRecord.is_receptor == True)  # noqa: E712 - SQL expression
        ).all()
    misfits: list[int] = []
    for receptor, site in rows:
        box = site_payload(site)
        if box is None:
            continue
        with self._receptor_as_pdb(receptor) as readable:  # mmCIF too: the Zn check reads PDB columns
            if readable is not None and excludes(method, readable, box["center"], box["size"]):
                misfits.append(int(receptor.id))
    return misfits

def list_box_residues(self, *, receptor_id: int, engine: str = "vina") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Residues with at least one atom inside the receptor's active binding-site box.

    Candidate set for flexible-residue selection — short because the box filters it.
    Returns [] when there's no active grid or the structure file is unavailable.
    """
    grid = self.get_grid(receptor_id=int(receptor_id), engine=engine)
    if grid is None:
        return []
    center = tuple(float(v) for v in grid.get("center") or [])
    size = tuple(float(v) for v in grid.get("size") or [])
    if len(center) != 3 or len(size) != 3:
        return []
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        receptor = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(receptor_id))
    if receptor is None:
        return []
    try:
        with self._receptor_as_pdb(receptor) as readable_receptor:
            if readable_receptor is None:
                return []
            residues = residues_in_box(
                readable_receptor.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"), center, size
            )
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return []
    return [
        {"key": r.key, "label": r.label, "chain": r.chain, "resname": r.resname, "resnum": r.resnum}
        for r in residues
    ]

check_required materializes the full ligand set to report missing ligands; that's the expensive part. The Receptors step only shows receptor prep/grid status, so this skips ligands entirely (receptor sets are small).

Source code in src/amdockvs/docking/api.py 
def check_receptors(
        self,
        *,
        program: str = VINA_PROGRAM.key,
        receptor_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Receptor-only half of check_required: preparation + grid status, no ligand scan.

    check_required materializes the full ligand set to report missing ligands; that's
    the expensive part. The Receptors step only shows receptor prep/grid status, so this
    skips ligands entirely (receptor sets are small).
    """
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    program_spec = self.get_program_spec(program)
    receptor_set_ref = (
        None
        if receptor_set is None or is_molecule_scope(receptor_set)
        else ensure_molecule_set_ref(self.runtime, receptor_set, name="docking_check_receptor_input")
    )
    receptor_scope = scope_payload(receptor_set) if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else {}
    receptor_filters = self._program_scope_filters(receptor_scope, role="receptor", program=program_spec)
    receptor_rows = list_entity_rows(
        self.runtime.workspace.project_db,
        entity_kind="receptor",
        engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        filters=receptor_filters,
        fields=("id", "prepared_engine", "grid_engine"),
        order=("id",),
    )
    receptor_ids = [int(row.get("id") or 0) for row in receptor_rows if int(row.get("id") or 0) > 0]
    ready_prepared = {
        int(row.get("id") or 0)
        for row in receptor_rows
        if not program_spec.requires_receptor_preparation or bool(row.get("prepared_engine"))
    }
    ready_grid = {
        int(row.get("id") or 0)
        for row in receptor_rows
        if not program_spec.requires_binding_site or bool(row.get("grid_engine"))
    }
    return {
        "receptor_ids": receptor_ids,
        "missing": {
            "receptors_prepared": [rid for rid in receptor_ids if rid not in ready_prepared],
            "receptor_binding_sites": [rid for rid in receptor_ids if rid not in ready_grid],
        },
        "counts": {
            "receptors_total": len(receptor_rows),
            "receptors_ready": len(ready_prepared),
            "receptor_grids_ready": len(ready_grid),
        },
    }

def run(
        self,
        *,
        program: str = VINA_PROGRAM.key,
        ligands: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | Selection[MoleculeRecord] | int | None = None,
        receptors: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | Selection[MoleculeRecord] | int | None = None,
        ligand_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
        receptor_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
        output_dir: PathLike | None = None,
        batch_size: int | None = None,
        exhaustiveness: int = 8,
        num_modes: int = 9,
        box_center: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
        box_size: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
        scoring_function: str = "vina",
        vina_backend: str = DEFAULT_VINA_BACKEND,
        vina_command: str = DEFAULT_VINA_COMMAND,
        vina_cpu: int = 1,
        seed: int = 0,
        spacing: float = 0.375,
        energy_range: float = 3.0,
        min_rmsd: float = 1.0,
        run_id: str | None = None,
        protocol_metadata: dict | None = None,
        engine_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
        depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
        check_required: bool = True,
        skip_existing: bool = True,
        compute_interactions: bool = False,
        hit_threshold: float | None = None,
        hit_cap: int = 0,
        payload: str = PAYLOAD_LIGHT,
        selected_from_receptor_id: int | None = None,
        selected_top_n: int | None = None,
        selected_max_score: float | None = None,
        replace_existing: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Run docking over the active library, selecting its row or shard adapter.

    ``hit_threshold``/``hit_cap`` are optional for materialized rows and mandatory for a
    sharded library, where returning every scored molecule would defeat the storage model.
    ``compute_interactions`` finds each pose's interactions in the chunk that docked it.
    An off-target stage sets ``selected_from_receptor_id``/``selected_top_n``: the other
    receptors dock only that receptor's Top-N ligands, read when the job starts — so it
    `depends_on` the target's job. Over rows, ``selected_max_score`` keeps only those at
    or below it (a sharded library uses ``hit_threshold`` for that).
    """
    if selected_top_n is not None and selected_from_receptor_id is None:
        raise ValueError("selected_top_n requires selected_from_receptor_id.")
    if ligands is not None:
        if ligand_set is not None:
            raise ValueError("Pass either ligands or ligand_set, not both.")
        ligand_set = ligands
    if receptors is not None:
        if receptor_set is not None:
            raise ValueError("Pass either receptors or receptor_set, not both.")
        receptor_set = receptors
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    knobs = dict(
        exhaustiveness=exhaustiveness,
        num_modes=num_modes,
        scoring_function=scoring_function,
        vina_backend=vina_backend,
        vina_command=vina_command,
        vina_cpu=vina_cpu,
        seed=seed,
        spacing=spacing,
        energy_range=energy_range,
        min_rmsd=min_rmsd,
    )
    if ligand_set is None and has_shards(self.runtime.workspace.project_db):
        if hit_threshold is None or int(hit_cap) <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "docking.run over a sharded library requires hit_threshold and hit_cap."
            )
        if compute_interactions:
            raise ValueError(
                "compute_interactions is not available during sharded docking; compute "
                "interactions after hits have been materialized."
            )
        return self.run_shards(
            program=program,
            receptor_set=receptor_set,
            hit_threshold=float(hit_threshold),
            hit_cap=int(hit_cap),
            output_dir=output_dir,
            box_center=box_center,
            box_size=box_size,
            **knobs,
            run_id=run_id,
            protocol_metadata=protocol_metadata,
            engine_config=engine_config,
            executor_name=executor_name,
            depends_on=depends_on,
            skip_existing=skip_existing,
            payload=payload,
            check_required=check_required,
            selected_from_receptor_id=selected_from_receptor_id,
            selected_top_n=selected_top_n,
            replace_existing=replace_existing,
        )
    if selected_from_receptor_id is not None and not selected_top_n:
        raise ValueError("An off-target stage over ligand rows requires selected_top_n.")
    if hit_cap and hit_threshold is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "docking.run needs hit_threshold when hit_cap is set: the threshold is the "
            "scientific criterion, the cap is only what makes the run end."
        )
    program_spec = self.get_program_spec(program)
    resolved_engine_config = _validated_engine_config(program_spec, engine_config, **knobs)
    protocol_metadata = self.check_protocol(
        program=program_spec.key, engine_config=resolved_engine_config,
        protocol_metadata=protocol_metadata, replace_existing=replace_existing,
    )
    reset_results = replace_existing and check_protocol_conflict(
        self.runtime.workspace.project_db, program=program_spec, protocol=protocol_metadata, replace_existing=True,
    )
    if reset_results and selected_from_receptor_id is not None:
        raise ValueError("Changing docking configuration requires rerunning the reference stage before off-target docking.")
    resolved_batch_size = max(1, int(batch_size or app_config(self.runtime).docking.batch_size))
    ligand_set_ref = self._set_ref(ligand_set, name="docking_ligand_input")
    receptor_set_ref = self._set_ref(receptor_set, name="docking_receptor_input")
    ligand_scope = scope_payload(ligand_set) if is_molecule_scope(ligand_set) else {}
    receptor_scope = scope_payload(receptor_set) if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else {}
    ligand_filters = self._program_scope_filters(ligand_scope, role="ligand", program=program_spec)
    receptor_filters = self._program_scope_filters(receptor_scope, role="receptor", program=program_spec)
    if box_center is None or box_size is None:
        resolved_grid = self._grid_from_receptor_source(
            receptor_set if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else receptor_set_ref,
            engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        )
        if resolved_grid is not None:
            box_center, box_size, knobs["spacing"] = resolved_grid
    if (box_center is None) ^ (box_size is None):
        raise ValueError("docking.run requires both box_center and box_size when either one is provided.")
    # Always resolve counts: they gate readiness (when requested) AND give the true
    # chunk total so progress is computed against the real pair count instead of
    # completed/emitted-so-far (a lazy generator otherwise leaves total_chunks unknown,
    # making progress hover near 50-60% regardless of actual completion).
    requirement_check = self.check_required(
        program=program_spec.key,
        ligand_set=ligand_set if is_molecule_scope(ligand_set) else ligand_set_ref,
        receptor_set=receptor_set if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else receptor_set_ref,
    )
    if check_required and not bool(requirement_check.get("ready")):
        raise RuntimeError(_requirements_message(program_spec.key, requirement_check))
    run_counts = dict(requirement_check.get("counts") or {})
    # The docking feed pairs every prepared ligand with every prepared receptor
    # (receptors without a grid still emit a failed-pair chunk), batched by batch_size.
    total_pairs = int(run_counts.get("ligands_ready") or 0) * int(run_counts.get("receptors_ready") or 0)
    if check_required and total_pairs <= 0:
        # Fail early and clearly instead of submitting a job whose feed yields no pairs
        # (which would otherwise complete silently with zero results).
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"docking.run has no valid ligand-receptor pairs to dock for docking.{program_spec.key}: "
            f"counts={run_counts}. Import and prepare at least one ligand and one receptor first."
        )
    # The feed applies skip_existing after resolving the scoped cross-product. Its declared
    # total must use that same filtered count; over-declaring makes Molsuite wait forever for
    # chunks that the feed intentionally never emits.
    pending_pairs = count_pending_docking_pairs(
        project_db=self.runtime.workspace.project_db,
        engine=program_spec.docking_engine,
        preparation_engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        ligand_set_id=None if ligand_set_ref is None else int(ligand_set_ref.id),
        receptor_set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        ligand_filters=ligand_filters,
        receptor_filters=receptor_filters,
        protocol_metadata=protocol_metadata,
        skip_existing=False if reset_results else skip_existing,
        requires_ligand_preparation=program_spec.requires_ligand_preparation,
        requires_receptor_preparation=program_spec.requires_receptor_preparation,
    )
    # The Top-N does not exist yet when an off-target stage is submitted: declare nothing
    # (a floor of 0) rather than a count that could over-declare and never complete.
    total_chunks = (
        -(-pending_pairs // resolved_batch_size)
        if pending_pairs > 0 and selected_from_receptor_id is None else 0
    )
    params = DockingJobParams(
        output_dir=self._output_dir(output_dir),
        batch_size=resolved_batch_size,
        row_batch_size=batch_size_for("ligand", self.runtime),
        ligand_set_id=None if ligand_set_ref is None else int(ligand_set_ref.id),
        receptor_set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        ligand_filters=ligand_filters,
        receptor_filters=receptor_filters,
        engine=program_spec.docking_engine,
        preparation_engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        requires_ligand_preparation=program_spec.requires_ligand_preparation,
        requires_receptor_preparation=program_spec.requires_receptor_preparation,
        requires_binding_site=program_spec.requires_binding_site,
        box_center=box_center,
        box_size=box_size,
        **_engine_fields(resolved_engine_config, knobs),
        run_id=str(run_id or uuid4().hex),
        protocol_metadata=dict(protocol_metadata or {}),
        engine_config=resolved_engine_config,
        skip_existing=skip_existing,
        hit_threshold=hit_threshold,
        hit_cap=max(0, int(hit_cap)),
        interactions=bool(compute_interactions),
        selected_from_receptor_id=selected_from_receptor_id,
        selected_top_n=selected_top_n,
        selected_max_score=selected_max_score,
    )
    if reset_results:
        clear_previous_docking(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, program=program_spec)
    job_id = self.runtime.submit_job(
        docking_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        # Each docking chunk runs one engine process that uses `vina_cpu` threads
        # internally, so reserve that many CPU tokens from the pool to avoid
        # oversubscription (pool limits concurrency to floor(cpus / vina_cpu)).
        cpu_required=program_spec.resource_requirements(resolved_engine_config)["cpu_required"],
        # Declare the real chunk total so progress = processed/total (not processed/emitted).
        total_chunks=total_chunks,
    )
    return job_id

def compute_diagrams(
        self,
        *,
        result_ids: list[int] | None = None,
        run_id: str = "",

    """Render 2D interaction diagrams for docking poses as a standalone job.

    is written to the DB, so re-run with ``replace_existing=True`` to refresh.
    """
    self.runtime._require_active_project()

        result_ids=[int(value) for value in (result_ids or []) if int(value) > 0],

        score_lte=score_lte,
        pose_rank=pose_rank,
        fmt=str(fmt or "png"),
        chunk_size=max(1, int(chunk_size)),
        replace_existing=bool(replace_existing),
    )
    return self.runtime.submit_job(
        diagram_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
    )

cluster_job(*, method: str = 'bitbirch', threshold: float = 0.65, per_cluster: int = 1, molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | int | None = None, molecule_filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, fp_radius: int = 2, fp_nbits: int = 2048, with_activity: str = '', cluster_run_id: str = '', num_cpus: int | None = None, executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR, depends_on: list[str] | None = None, shards: bool = False) -> str

Submit the clustering job over the DB; results land in clustering_results. Returns the job id. The run is tagged with cluster_run_id (auto if blank) — read it back with list_runs / get_run or persist its centroids with save_centroids_as_set. with_activity (an activity endpoint) narrows the scope to the ligands measured for it.

Each cluster starts with its per_cluster centroid-nearest members as representatives; pick_representatives chooses again, by any mode, without clustering again.

num_cpus sets the parallelism: >1 runs bblean multiround with that many processes and the job requests exactly that many CPUs (cpu_required) so mf schedules it correctly. When None it is derived from the scope size via plan_cpus.

shards clusters the library's shards instead (the scope arguments do not apply): a fingerprint job packs them shard by shard, the clustering waits for it, and only the representatives become molecule rows; every member stays in the run's sidecar by io.shards.shard_key. Both jobs run at SHARDS_PRIORITY.

def cluster_job(
    self,
    *,
    method: str = "bitbirch",
    threshold: float = 0.65,
    per_cluster: int = 1,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | int | None = None,
    molecule_filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
    with_activity: str = "",
    cluster_run_id: str = "",
    num_cpus: int | None = None,
    executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    shards: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Submit the clustering job over the DB; results land in ``clustering_results``. Returns
    the job id. The run is tagged with ``cluster_run_id`` (auto if blank) — read it back with
    ``list_runs`` / ``get_run`` or persist its centroids with ``save_centroids_as_set``.
    ``with_activity`` (an activity endpoint) narrows the scope to the ligands measured for it.

    Each cluster starts with its ``per_cluster`` centroid-nearest members as representatives;
    ``pick_representatives`` chooses again, by any mode, without clustering again.

    ``num_cpus`` sets the parallelism: >1 runs bblean multiround with that many processes and the
    job **requests exactly that many CPUs** (``cpu_required``) so mf schedules it correctly. When
    None it is derived from the scope size via ``plan_cpus``.

    ``shards`` clusters the library's shards instead (the scope arguments do not apply): a
    fingerprint job packs them shard by shard, the clustering waits for it, and only the
    representatives become molecule rows; every member stays in the run's sidecar by
    ``io.shards.shard_key``. Both jobs run at ``SHARDS_PRIORITY``."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    if num_cpus is None and shards:
        num_cpus = plan_cpus(ShardStore(self.runtime.workspace.project_db).record_count())
    if num_cpus is None:
        num_cpus = plan_cpus(
            self.scope_count(
                molecule_set=molecule_set, molecule_filters=molecule_filters,
                fp_radius=fp_radius, fp_nbits=fp_nbits, with_activity=with_activity,
            )
        )
    num_cpus = max(1, int(num_cpus))
    params = SelectionClusterJobParams(
        batch_size=app_config(self.runtime).diversity.rows_per_task,
        method=method,
        threshold=threshold,
        per_cluster=per_cluster,
        molecule_set_id=None if molecule_set is None else int(getattr(molecule_set, "id", molecule_set)),
        molecule_filters=dict(molecule_filters or {}),
        fp_radius=fp_radius,
        fp_nbits=fp_nbits,
        with_activity=with_activity,
        cluster_run_id=cluster_run_id or uuid.uuid4().hex,
        num_processes=num_cpus,
        shards=shards,
    )
    priority = {}
    if shards:
        priority = {"priority": SHARDS_PRIORITY}
        depends_on = [self.runtime.submit_job(
            shard_fingerprints_job, params=params.model_dump(mode="python"), executor_name=executor_name,
            depends_on=depends_on, **priority,
        )]
    return self.runtime.submit_job(
        cluster_molecules_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        cpu_required=num_cpus,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        **priority,
    )

Load a scope's fingerprint matrix + 2-D projection for the interactive view. Samples a random sample_limit subset (seeded by seed so each preview draws a fresh subset), skipping exclude_ids (molecules already previewed) so repeated previews cover more of the space. Projects onto basis when given (a prior preview's fitted PCA axes) so runs overlay in one comparable space; otherwise fits a new basis and returns it. Heavy (DB read + PCA); call off the GUI thread. Cheap re-clustering then uses cluster_loaded.

Source code in src/amdockvs/diversity/api.py 
def load_universe(
    self,
    *,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | int | None = None,
    molecule_filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
    sample_limit: int = DEFAULT_SAMPLE_LIMIT,
    seed: int = 0,
    basis: Any = None,
    exclude_ids: Any = None,
) -> UniverseMatrix:
    """Load a scope's fingerprint matrix + 2-D projection for the interactive view. Samples a
    random ``sample_limit`` subset (seeded by ``seed`` so each preview draws a *fresh* subset),
    skipping ``exclude_ids`` (molecules already previewed) so repeated previews cover more of
    the space. Projects onto ``basis`` when given (a prior preview's fitted PCA axes) so runs
    overlay in one comparable space; otherwise fits a new basis and returns it. Heavy (DB read +
    PCA); call off the GUI thread. Cheap re-clustering then uses ``cluster_loaded``."""
    import random

    from amdockvs.diversity.clustering import fit_project_2d, fp_matrix_from_bitstrings, project_2d_onto

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    params = SelectionClusterJobParams(
        batch_size=app_config(self.runtime).diversity.rows_per_task,
        molecule_set_id=None if molecule_set is None else int(getattr(molecule_set, "id", molecule_set)),
        molecule_filters=dict(molecule_filters or {}),
        fp_radius=fp_radius,
        fp_nbits=fp_nbits,
    )
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    skip = {int(i) for i in (exclude_ids or ())}
    rows, total, eligible = _reservoir_sample(
        scope_molecule_rows(project_db, params),
        limit=int(sample_limit),
        seed=int(seed),
        skip=skip,
    )
    sampled = eligible > int(sample_limit)
    stored = stored_fingerprints_for_ids(
        project_db, [int(r["id"]) for r in rows], radius=fp_radius, nbits=fp_nbits
    )
    ordered_ids: list[int] = []
    bitstrings: list[bytes] = []
    for row in rows:
        mol_id = int(row["id"])
        fp = stored.get(mol_id) or _fingerprint_from_structure(project_db, row, radius=fp_radius, nbits=fp_nbits)
        if fp is None:
            continue
        ordered_ids.append(mol_id)
        bitstrings.append(fp)
    x_matrix = fp_matrix_from_bitstrings(bitstrings)
    if basis is None:
        projection, evr, basis = fit_project_2d(x_matrix)
    else:
        projection, evr = project_2d_onto(x_matrix, basis), list(basis.get("evr") or [0.0, 0.0])
    return UniverseMatrix(
        molecule_ids=ordered_ids,
        x_matrix=x_matrix,
        projection=[[float(x), float(y)] for x, y in projection],
        projection_variance=list(evr),
        total_in_scope=total,
        sampled=sampled,
        basis=basis,
    )

@staticmethod
def cluster_loaded(
    universe: UniverseMatrix,
    *,
    method: str = "bitbirch",
    per_cluster: int = 1,
    **method_params: Any,
) -> AnalysisResult:
    """Cluster an already-loaded ``UniverseMatrix`` — the cheap step that re-runs on every knob
    change without touching the DB. ``method_params`` (threshold, batch_size, …) go straight to
    the registered method, so each method's own knobs pass through untouched."""
    threshold = float(method_params.get("threshold", 0.65))
    if not universe.molecule_ids:
        return AnalysisResult(
            [], [], [], {"n_clusters": 0, "n_molecules": 0, "clusters": []}, [], [0.0, 0.0],
            method, threshold, universe.total_in_scope, universe.sampled,
        )
    result = cluster_and_select(
        universe.x_matrix, method=method, per_cluster=per_cluster, with_projection=False, **method_params
    )
    rep_ids = [universe.molecule_ids[i] for i in result.representative_indices]
    return AnalysisResult(
        molecule_ids=universe.molecule_ids,
        labels=[int(v) for v in result.labels],
        representative_ids=rep_ids,
        stats=result.stats,
        projection=universe.projection,
        projection_variance=universe.projection_variance,
        method=method,
        threshold=threshold,
        total_in_scope=universe.total_in_scope,
        sampled=universe.sampled,
    )

Cluster the ENTIRE scope (no sampling) and pick representatives — the real 'run the selection' behind the interactive Preview. Every molecule's fingerprint is loaded and clustered (bblean is fast); only the 2-D graph basis is fitted on a random sub-sample and every point projected onto it (cheap), so the plot scales without the full-N SVD. Returns the same mapping as cluster_loaded, over the whole scope. Heavy — call off the GUI thread. Raises if the scope exceeds INLINE_RUN_LIMIT (that needs the parallel job).

Source code in src/amdockvs/diversity/api.py 
def run_selection(
    self,
    *,
    method: str = "bitbirch",
    per_cluster: int = 1,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | int | None = None,
    molecule_filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
    **method_params: Any,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Cluster the ENTIRE scope (no sampling) and pick representatives — the real 'run the
    selection' behind the interactive Preview. Every molecule's fingerprint is loaded and
    clustered (bblean is fast); only the 2-D graph basis is fitted on a random sub-sample and
    every point projected onto it (cheap), so the plot scales without the full-N SVD. Returns the
    same mapping as ``cluster_loaded``, over the whole scope. Heavy — call off the GUI thread.
    Raises if the scope exceeds ``INLINE_RUN_LIMIT`` (that needs the parallel job)."""
    import random

    from amdockvs.diversity.clustering import (
        fit_project_2d,
        fp_matrix_from_bitstrings,
        project_2d_onto,
    )

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    params = SelectionClusterJobParams(
        batch_size=app_config(self.runtime).diversity.rows_per_task,
        molecule_set_id=None if molecule_set is None else int(getattr(molecule_set, "id", molecule_set)),
        molecule_filters=dict(molecule_filters or {}),
        fp_radius=fp_radius,
        fp_nbits=fp_nbits,
    )
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    # Stop one row past the limit instead of loading the scope first: a scope too big for the
    # inline path must not be materialized just to be rejected.
    rows = list(islice(scope_molecule_rows(project_db, params), INLINE_RUN_LIMIT + 1))
    if len(rows) > INLINE_RUN_LIMIT:
        raise ValueError(
            f"More than {INLINE_RUN_LIMIT} molecules exceed the serial limit — this scope belongs "
            f"on the parallel clustering job (cluster_job), not the inline path."
        )
    total = len(rows)
    stored = stored_fingerprints_for_ids(
        project_db, [int(r["id"]) for r in rows], radius=fp_radius, nbits=fp_nbits
    )
    ordered_ids: list[int] = []
    bitstrings: list[bytes] = []
    for row in rows:
        mol_id = int(row["id"])
        fp = stored.get(mol_id) or _fingerprint_from_structure(project_db, row, radius=fp_radius, nbits=fp_nbits)
        if fp is None:
            continue
        ordered_ids.append(mol_id)
        bitstrings.append(fp)
    x_matrix = fp_matrix_from_bitstrings(bitstrings)
    universe = UniverseMatrix(
        molecule_ids=ordered_ids, x_matrix=x_matrix, projection=[],
        projection_variance=[0.0, 0.0], total_in_scope=total, sampled=False,
    )
    n = len(ordered_ids)
    if n:
        fit_idx = list(range(n))
        if n > PROJECT_FIT_SAMPLE:
            fit_idx = random.Random(0).sample(fit_idx, PROJECT_FIT_SAMPLE)
        _coords, evr, basis = fit_project_2d(x_matrix[fit_idx])
        proj = project_2d_onto(x_matrix, basis)
        universe.projection = [[float(x), float(y)] for x, y in proj]
        universe.projection_variance = list(evr)
    return self.cluster_loaded(
        universe, method=method, per_cluster=per_cluster, **method_params
    ).to_mapping()

Register a finished parallel run as a saved result WITHOUT recomputing anything: the job's task already wrote the graph sidecar <root>/clustering_runs/<run_id>.parquet (PCA points + cluster/centroid flags). Read it for the counts + aggregated cluster sizes and insert the compact ClusteringRun summary pointing at it. No fingerprints, no PCA here.

Source code in src/amdockvs/diversity/api.py 
def register_run_from_sidecar(
    self,
    cluster_run_id: str,
    *,
    method: str,
    threshold: float,
    scope_label: str,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
) -> str:
    """Register a finished parallel run as a saved result WITHOUT recomputing anything: the job's
    task already wrote the graph sidecar ``<root>/clustering_runs/<run_id>.parquet`` (PCA points +
    cluster/centroid flags). Read it for the counts + aggregated cluster sizes and insert the
    compact ``ClusteringRun`` summary pointing at it. No fingerprints, no PCA here."""
    import pandas as pd

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    snapshot = self._project_root() / "clustering_runs" / f"{cluster_run_id}.parquet"
    if snapshot.exists():
        frame = pd.read_parquet(snapshot)
        n_molecules = int(len(frame))
        n_clusters = int(frame["cluster_id"].nunique()) if n_molecules else 0
        n_reps = int(frame["is_centroid"].sum()) if n_molecules else 0
        cluster_stats = [
            {"cluster_id": int(cid), "size": int(size), "tightness": 0.0}
            for cid, size in frame.groupby("cluster_id").size().items()
        ]
        snapshot_path = str(snapshot)
    else:  # sidecar missing (e.g. write failed) → counts-only summary, no graph
        n_molecules = n_clusters = n_reps = 0
        cluster_stats = []
        snapshot_path = ""
    row = ClusteringRun(
        run_id=cluster_run_id, method=str(method), threshold=float(threshold),
        scope_label=str(scope_label), fp_radius=int(fp_radius), fp_nbits=int(fp_nbits),
        n_molecules=n_molecules, n_clusters=n_clusters, n_reps=n_reps,
        snapshot_path=snapshot_path, evr=[0.0, 0.0], cluster_stats=cluster_stats,
    )
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        session.add(row)
        session.commit()
    return cluster_run_id

def list_runs(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Persisted clustering runs, newest first: run id, method, cluster/centroid counts."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        rows = session.exec(select(ClusteringResult).order_by(ClusteringResult.id)).all()
    runs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        entry = runs.setdefault(
            row.cluster_run_id,
            {"cluster_run_id": row.cluster_run_id, "method": row.method,
             "n_molecules": 0, "n_clusters": set(), "n_centroids": 0},
        )
        entry["n_molecules"] += 1
        entry["n_clusters"].add(int(row.cluster_id))
        if row.is_centroid:
            entry["n_centroids"] += 1
    out = []
    for entry in runs.values():
        entry["n_clusters"] = len(entry["n_clusters"])
        out.append(entry)
    return out[::-1]  # runs in order of their first row: newest first

pick_representatives(cluster_run_id: str, *, mode: str = 'centroid', per_cluster: int = 1, fraction: float = 0.1, rank_by: str = '') -> dict[str, int]

Choose again what represents each cluster of a finished run. Nothing is clustered again: the run already ranks every member, and this only reads that ranking (modes: see clustering.pick_representatives). rank_by (an activity endpoint) replaces similarity as what 'extremes' / 'quartiles' / 'proportional' spread over. Rewrites the run's representative flags; returns {"n_molecules", "n_clusters", "n_reps"}.

ponytail: in-process over the run's columns (~20 B/molecule) and one UPDATE per 900 picks. Make it a job when a run outgrows the tens of millions.

Source code in src/amdockvs/diversity/api.py 
def pick_representatives(
    self,
    cluster_run_id: str,
    *,
    mode: str = "centroid",
    per_cluster: int = 1,
    fraction: float = 0.1,
    rank_by: str = "",
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Choose again what represents each cluster of a finished run. Nothing is clustered
    again: the run already ranks every member, and this only reads that ranking (modes:
    see ``clustering.pick_representatives``). ``rank_by`` (an activity endpoint) replaces
    similarity as what 'extremes' / 'quartiles' / 'proportional' spread over. Rewrites the
    run's representative flags; returns {"n_molecules", "n_clusters", "n_reps"}.

    ponytail: in-process over the run's columns (~20 B/molecule) and one UPDATE per 900
    picks. Make it a job when a run outgrows the tens of millions."""
    import pandas as pd

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    run_id = str(cluster_run_id)
    sidecar = self._project_root() / "clustering_runs" / f"{run_id}.parquet"
    frame = pd.read_parquet(sidecar) if sidecar.exists() else None
    if frame is None or "similarity" not in frame:
        raise ValueError("This run keeps no member rankings (it predates them): cluster again once.")
    values = None
    if rank_by:
        activity = activity_values(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, rank_by)
        values = frame["molecule_id"].map(activity).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    labels = frame["cluster_id"].to_numpy()
    picks = pick_representatives(
        labels, frame["similarity"].to_numpy(), mode=mode, per_cluster=per_cluster, fraction=fraction,
        centrality=frame["centrality"].to_numpy(), values=values,
    )
    flags = np.zeros(len(frame), dtype=bool)
    flags[picks] = True
    picked_ids = [int(i) for i in frame["molecule_id"].to_numpy()[picks]]
    of_run = ClusteringResult.cluster_run_id == run_id
    if picked_ids and is_shard_key(picked_ids[0]):
        picked_ids = self._promote_picks(run_id, picked_ids, labels[picks])
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        session.exec(sql_update(ClusteringResult).where(of_run).values(is_centroid=False))
        for start in range(0, len(picked_ids), 900):
            session.exec(
                sql_update(ClusteringResult)
                .where(of_run, ClusteringResult.molecule_id.in_(picked_ids[start:start + 900]))
                .values(is_centroid=True)
            )
        session.exec(sql_update(ClusteringRun).where(ClusteringRun.run_id == run_id).values(n_reps=len(picks)))
        session.commit()
    frame["is_centroid"] = flags
    frame.to_parquet(sidecar, index=False)
    return {"n_molecules": len(frame), "n_clusters": int(len(np.unique(labels))), "n_reps": len(picks)}

def members_clause(self, cluster_run_id: str, cluster_id: int | None = None):
    """Opaque SmartTable adapter: the molecules of one cluster, or the run's representatives
    when no cluster is given. A subquery, so it costs the same for 10 members or 10^6."""
    picked = select(ClusteringResult.molecule_id).where(
        ClusteringResult.cluster_run_id == str(cluster_run_id)
    )
    if cluster_id is None:
        picked = picked.where(ClusteringResult.is_centroid == True)  # noqa: E712 - SQL, not Python
    else:
        picked = picked.where(ClusteringResult.cluster_id == int(cluster_id))
    return MoleculeRecord.id.in_(picked)

def exclude_non_representatives(self, cluster_run_id: str) -> int:
    """Mark every non-representative of a run as excluded (the flag Filter uses; reversible).
    Returns how many were marked."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    non_reps = [r["molecule_id"] for r in self.get_run(cluster_run_id) if not r["is_centroid"]]
    if not non_reps:
        return 0
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        run = session.exec(select(ClusteringRun).where(ClusteringRun.run_id == str(cluster_run_id))).first()
    detail = f"{run.method}, t={run.threshold}" if run is not None else str(cluster_run_id)[:8]
    return int(self.runtime.molecules.set_excluded_state(
        non_reps, excluded=True, reason=f"diversity: non-representative ({detail})"
    ))

items.title: save_clustering_result
items.text:
save_clustering_result(*, points: Iterable[tuple], cluster_stats: list[dict[str, Any]], evr: Iterable[float], method: str, threshold: float, scope_label: str, fp_radius: int = 2, fp_nbits: int = 2048, n_molecules: int | None = None, n_clusters: int | None = None, n_reps: int | None = None) -> str

Persist an applied clustering as a durable run: the graph points (x, y, molecule_id, cluster_id, is_centroid) to a parquet sidecar, and a compact ClusteringRun row (metadata + counts + the sidecar path). Returns the run id. Only the PCA + cluster flags are stored — fingerprints stay in their table, loaded by id if ever needed. Counts default to what the points imply; the parallel path passes them explicitly (it saves no graph sidecar yet).

Source code in src/amdockvs/diversity/api.py 
def save_clustering_result(
    self,
    *,
    points: Iterable[tuple],
    cluster_stats: list[dict[str, Any]],
    evr: Iterable[float],
    method: str,
    threshold: float,
    scope_label: str,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
    n_molecules: int | None = None,
    n_clusters: int | None = None,
    n_reps: int | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Persist an applied clustering as a durable run: the graph points (x, y, molecule_id,
    cluster_id, is_centroid) to a parquet sidecar, and a compact ``ClusteringRun`` row (metadata
    + counts + the sidecar path). Returns the run id. Only the PCA + cluster flags are stored —
    fingerprints stay in their table, loaded by id if ever needed. Counts default to what the
    points imply; the parallel path passes them explicitly (it saves no graph sidecar yet)."""
    import pandas as pd

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
    snap_dir = self._project_root() / "clustering_runs"
    snap_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    snapshot = snap_dir / f"{run_id}.parquet"
    frame = pd.DataFrame(
        list(points), columns=["x", "y", "molecule_id", "cluster_id", "is_centroid"]
    )
    frame.to_parquet(snapshot, index=False)
    row = ClusteringRun(
        run_id=run_id, method=str(method), threshold=float(threshold), scope_label=str(scope_label),
        fp_radius=int(fp_radius), fp_nbits=int(fp_nbits),
        n_molecules=int(n_molecules if n_molecules is not None else len(frame)),
        n_clusters=int(n_clusters if n_clusters is not None else len(cluster_stats or [])),
        n_reps=int(n_reps if n_reps is not None else (frame["is_centroid"].sum() if len(frame) else 0)),
        snapshot_path=str(snapshot), evr=list(evr or [0.0, 0.0]), cluster_stats=list(cluster_stats or []),
    )
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        session.add(row)
        session.commit()
    return run_id

load_clustering_result(run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]

Everything needed to redraw a saved run (graph points + cluster stats + evr) — read the sidecar directly, no re-clustering or PCA recompute.

Source code in src/amdockvs/diversity/api.py 
def load_clustering_result(self, run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Everything needed to redraw a saved run (graph points + cluster stats + evr) — read the
    sidecar directly, no re-clustering or PCA recompute."""
    import pandas as pd

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        row = session.exec(select(ClusteringRun).where(ClusteringRun.run_id == str(run_id))).first()
    if row is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown clustering run: {run_id}")
    if row.snapshot_path and Path(row.snapshot_path).exists():
        frame = pd.read_parquet(row.snapshot_path)
    else:
        frame = pd.DataFrame(columns=["x", "y", "molecule_id", "cluster_id", "is_centroid"])
    return {
        "run_id": row.run_id, "method": row.method, "threshold": row.threshold,
        "scope_label": row.scope_label, "n_molecules": row.n_molecules, "n_clusters": row.n_clusters,
        "n_reps": row.n_reps, "evr": list(row.evr or [0.0, 0.0]),
        "cluster_stats": list(row.cluster_stats or []), "points": frame.to_dict("records"),
    }

items.title: Modelo de ejecución del backend
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Una ruta pública, dos adaptadores
items.text:
El backend no tiene dos pipelines científicos. La biblioteca activa determina la unidad de trabajo:

Biblioteca Unidad entregada a MF Adaptador de E/S Molecules en la DB Lote de filas transform_ligand_rows Shards Uno o varios shards completos transform_ligand_shard

ChemistryAPI.run_ligand_pipeline, DockingAPI.prepare_ligands y DockingAPI.run seleccionan el adaptador automáticamente cuando no se proporciona un scope explícito de filas. Los métodos run_shard_pipeline, prepare_ligand_shards y run_shards siguen disponibles como primitivas internas y para llamadas especializadas.

MF recibe jobs y chunks normales. En HPC, compute puede corresponder al clúster Ray levantado dentro de una reserva; AMDock no genera arrays ni un submission del scheduler por shard.
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Qué significa “puro” aquí
items.text:
Se distinguen tres niveles. Es importante no llamar pura a una función sólo porque corre en un worker:

  1. Pura: depende únicamente de sus argumentos y no hace E/S.
  2. Kernel en memoria: no abre la DB ni administra archivos, pero puede usar aleatoriedad, librerías nativas o un backend externo.
  3. Adaptador: lee/escribe archivos, ejecuta programas o persiste estado.
Área Funciones principales Nivel Aplicación Composición química normalize_steps, kwargs_for, run_pipeline Kernel en memoria Una llamada continua por lote o shard Química RDKit standardize_ligand_molecule, generate_ligand_3d, minimize_ligand_molecule Kernel en memoria Pasos encadenables sin escritura intermedia Descriptores calculate_basic_descriptors Pura respecto al Mol Paralela por molécula/lote Fingerprints morgan_fingerprint, conversiones a bitstring/matriz Pura respecto al Mol Debe agruparse con descriptores cuando ambos se necesitan Clustering bitbirch_lean, select_representatives, cluster_stats, proyección PCA Pura sobre matrices Reducción global después de construir fingerprints Geometría del sitio centroid, radius_of_gyration, box_edge_from_rg, box_from_coords, residues_in_box Pura Inline o por receptor; no requiere job propio Identidad de protocolo protocol_identity, protocol_hash Pura Antes de enviar el job y al consultar receipts Métricas simples predicted_ki_m, predicted_pki, ligand_efficiency Pura En el mismo task que procesa el resultado de docking Shard químico read_shard, write_shard, transform_ligand_shard Adaptador Un shard entra y otro sale Preparación prepare_entities_rows, prepare_ligand_shard Adaptador Job independiente y reutilizable por familia de engine Docking run_docking_chunk, extract_ligands Adaptador Chunk distribuido por Ray; empaqueta resultados y sólo materializa hits en HTP P2Rank/interacciones/diagramas ejecutables y parsers respectivos Adaptador Jobs separados por dependencia y artefactos propios

run_pipeline es libre de DB y rutas, pero no es pureza matemática estricta: protonación puede invocar backends distintos y la generación 3D sólo es reproducible si conserva su semilla.
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Qué se agrupa continuamente
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Química de ligandos
items.text:
standardize -> protonate -> generate_3d -> minimize debe viajar como una lista de pasos en un único job. Cada task carga su lote o shard una vez, ejecuta toda la lista y escribe únicamente el resultado final. Enviar cuatro jobs separados implica cuatro lecturas, cuatro escrituras y tres barreras de sincronización innecesarias.

Los conformeros son una frontera. El modelo por filas puede materializar varios modelos, pero el formato actual de shard conserva una estructura por record. Por eso el backend rechaza conformers sobre shards en vez de perder silenciosamente el ensemble.
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Descriptores y fingerprints
items.text:
El job de descriptores ya puede calcular el fingerprint durante la misma lectura. Si ambos son necesarios, deben pedirse juntos. Calcular fingerprints como job independiente sólo es útil si:

  • los descriptores ya existen;
  • se necesita otra familia/radio de fingerprint; o
  • los fingerprints se producirán directamente desde shards para una reducción global.
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Diversity/BitBIRCH
items.text:
La creación de fingerprints es paralelizable por lote/shard. El clustering no es una colección de clusters independientes: necesita una reducción global. bblean multiround administra su propio paralelismo; desde MF debe verse como un job con los recursos reservados, no como miles de jobs pequeños.

La forma escalable es:

shards -> fingerprints parciales en paralelo -> manifiesto/matriz compacta -> clustering global
       -> selección de ids -> reconstrucción transaccional de shards
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Preparación y docking
items.text:
Permanecen como dos jobs lógicos porque la preparación es reutilizable entre receptores y protocolos. En una ejecución completamente remota ambos jobs deben correr dentro de la misma reserva Ray y sobre el mismo almacenamiento de trabajo; “dos jobs” no significa “dos reservas”.

La generación 3D puede ejecutarse antes como parte del pipeline químico. prepare_ligand_shard detecta conformaciones existentes y sólo genera 3D para los records que aún no las tienen.
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Resultados HTP
items.text:
El shard químico no cambia al prepararlo. ShardEngineState mantiene los artefactos por familia de preparación. ScreeningShardRun registra un receipt por run/shard/receptor/engine/protocolo; así un resume omite exactamente los pares terminados y no hereda el estado de otra campaña.

Cada task (shard, receptor) abre un fragmento Parquet de resultados y, después de cada ligando, añade una fila con score, métricas, SMILES y el SDF de todas las poses. En ese mismo punto elimina el PDBQT y, si no es hit, también el SDF suelto. El .results.parquet.tmp crece durante el trabajo y se publica atómicamente al terminar; por eso nunca se acumulan mil pares de archivos ni queda un shard final corrupto si el task falla. Los SDF individuales que sobreviven son sólo los hits que la UI necesita abrir. El receipt guarda la ruta del shard final.

El callback de MF recibe progreso por ligando y sirve también como punto de cancelación cooperativa para compute. En Ray la cancelación sigue siendo forzada por el propio adapter. Una campaña cancelada o fallida marca sus targets con ese estado y no promociona un top-N parcial.
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Dependencias y alcance diferido
items.text: El alcance de docking es una fotografía tomada una vez, pero se toma después de completar los jobs activos de importación, química y preparación. MF difiere build_chunks; en ese punto AMDock enumera los shards preparados, calcula el total definitivo y crea el plan de receptores. Esto evita tanto ignorar el último shard como hacer que el alcance cambie mientras una campaña ya está corriendo. No se consulta repetidamente una tabla “viva”.
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Fronteras que no deben fusionarse
items.text:
• La escritura del inventario y el cómputo del worker: el sink de MF persiste en el parent.
  • Preparación y docking cuando el artefacto preparado se reutilizará.
  • Fingerprints por shard y clustering global.
  • Docking y materialización completa: HTP sólo promueve hits.
  • Transformaciones sustitutivas de shards y borrado del conjunto anterior: primero se valida y activa el conjunto nuevo; después se elimina el anterior.

shards.keep_history controla si futuros rebuilders conservan los conjuntos sustituidos. El valor por defecto es false; aun así, el reemplazo debe ser transaccional y nunca borrar las entradas activas antes de que el nuevo conjunto esté completo.
path: Modelo de ejecución del backend

items.title: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock
items.text:
Este documento traduce el inventario de capacidades computacionales a una estructura de programación concreta.

No define todavía la UI. Define cómo debería organizarse el backend para que:

  • los cálculos comunes no queden enterrados en jobs;
  • las capacidades de dominio no se mezclen entre sí;
  • jobs/ quede como adaptación de ejecución y persistencia;
  • la UI consuma una estructura estable.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 1. Principio rector
items.text:
AMDock es ante todo un backend de cálculos químicos y computacionales.

Por lo tanto:

  • la arquitectura no debe partir de pantallas;
  • la arquitectura no debe partir de docks o workspaces;
  • la arquitectura debe partir de métodos comunes, capacidades y artefactos.

La UI debe reflejar esa estructura, no definirla.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 2. Regla de separación
items.text:
Usar esta regla simple:

  • si algo se reutiliza entre varios workflows, va a chemistry/;
  • si algo define una capacidad de negocio específica, va a su submódulo propio;
  • si algo sólo adapta a MolSuite/jobs/persistencia, va a jobs/;
  • si algo sólo representa o dispara acciones desde GUI, va a ui/.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 4. Rol de cada módulo principal
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 4.1 chemistry/
items.text:
Kernel químico compartido.

Aquí van métodos reutilizables por más de una capacidad:

  • lectura y normalización de moléculas;
  • generación de 3D/conformeros;
  • cálculo de descriptores;
  • cálculo de fingerprints;
  • similitud y subestructura;
  • alineamiento;
  • RMSD;
  • protonación y otras transformaciones generales.

chemistry/ no debe saber de PyMOL, de workspaces ni de jobs.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 4.2 docking/
items.text:
Lógica específica de docking y redocking:

  • preparación específica para el motor de docking;
  • definición de sitio/caja;
  • ejecución de docking;
  • scoring/rescoring;
  • redocking;
  • análisis de interacciones.

Puede depender de chemistry/, pero no al revés.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 4.3 qsar/
items.text:
Lógica específica de actividad, datasets y modelado:

  • actividad/endpoint;
  • ensamblado de matrices de features;
  • selección de features;
  • entrenamiento;
  • validación;
  • applicability domain;
  • predicción.

Puede depender de chemistry/, pero no al revés.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 4.4 analysis/
items.text:
Capacidades analíticas compartidas sobre resultados ya computados:

  • PCA;
  • clustering;
  • diversidad;
  • comparaciones y resúmenes exploratorios.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 4.5 jobs/
items.text:
Capa de integración con MolSuite/executor.

Aquí debería quedar sólo:

  • Params de ejecución;
  • wiring de @task y @job;
  • lectura/escritura de lotes;
  • llamadas a capacidades del backend real.

La ciencia principal no debería vivir aquí.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 5. Regla práctica de dependencia
items.text:
La dirección deseada es:

ui -> runtime -> jobs / queries / capacidades
jobs -> docking / qsar / chemistry / io
docking -> chemistry
qsar -> chemistry
analysis -> chemistry / qsar / docking
chemistry -> librerías científicas externas

Evitar:

chemistry -> docking
chemistry -> qsar
ui -> jobs directos
ui -> SQL o project_rows directo
jobs -> toda la lógica científica
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 6. Qué ya existe y qué conviene hacer primero
items.text:
Estado actual del árbol:

  • ya existen carpetas chemistry/, docking/, qsar/, analysis/
  • el código real todavía sigue concentrado sobre todo en:
  • io/loaders.py
  • jobs/descriptors.py
  • jobs/docking.py
  • jobs/ingestion.py

Por eso la migración recomendada no es reorganizar todo de golpe, sino extraer primero piezas compartidas y estables.

items.title: 9. Criterio para cerrar cada extracción
items.text:
Una pieza se considera bien migrada cuando:

  • tiene un módulo propio fuera de jobs/;
  • se puede importar y probar sin GUI;
  • no depende de MolSuite para su lógica central;
  • jobs/ sólo la llama, no la implementa;
  • el nombre del módulo refleja capacidad científica real.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: 10. Regla importante sobre nombres
items.text:
No usar Chem como módulo interno principal.

Motivo:

  • se confunde con rdkit.Chem;
  • no comunica si el módulo es de utilidades o de backend propio.

Preferir:

  • chemistry/
  • molecular/

En AMDock, chemistry/ parece el nombre más claro.
path: Guía de estructura modular del backend de AMDock

items.title: Inventario inicial de capacidades computacionales de AMDock
items.text:
Este documento define AMDock primero como motor de cálculo. No organiza pantallas ni docks; organiza qué cálculos existen, qué familias de métodos son comunes en CADD y qué piezas parecen transversales.

La intención es:

  • fijar el alcance científico/técnico del backend;
  • separar métodos comunes de métodos específicos;
  • preparar una estructura de módulos y artefactos que después la UI solo refleje.
path: Inventario inicial de capacidades computacionales de AMDock

items.title: 1. Cálculos que AMDock hará de forma explícita
path: Inventario inicial de capacidades computacionales de AMDock

items.title: 1.1 Docking
items.text:
Incluye:

  • preparación de receptor;
  • preparación de ligando;
  • generación/ajuste de conformaciones 3D si hace falta;
  • definición del sitio de unión;
  • docking convencional;
  • rescoring si aplica;
  • análisis de interacciones;
  • ranking y comparación de poses.
path: Inventario inicial de capacidades computacionales de AMDock

items.title: 1.2 Redocking
items.text:
Incluye todo lo de docking, con matices adicionales:

  • extracción del ligando nativo/co-cristalizado;
  • randomización o re-generación de la pose inicial;
  • redocking al mismo sitio;
  • comparación contra la pose cristalográfica;
  • RMSD de pose;
  • evaluación de capacidad de reproducción de pose;
  • eventualmente cross-docking como extensión natural.
path: Inventario inicial de capacidades computacionales de AMDock
